To this end, we propose a new worm spread model named SIHQR with time delay. Additionally, we establish a game model between susceptible and infected nodes in order to express the infection rate by several game parameters. Through analysis, we discuss the conditions for the emergence of three scenarios: disease-free equilibrium, endemic equilibrium and Hopf bifurcation. We study the stability at the equilibrium points and obtain an expression for a threshold value which determines whether the system exhibits endemic equilibrium or Hopf bifurcation. In the experimental section, we analyze the impact of initial values of node states and the magnitude of game parameters on worm spread in the three aforementioned scenarios. Finally, we propose a method to mitigate or even eliminate the Hopf bifurcation. The experimental results show that the proposed model has welldone performance.

title: Chapter 2: Mechanical and thermal energy storage technologies
Control based on the Koopman operator: A comprehensive review
abstract: The Koopman operator provides a powerful linear framework for analyzing nonlinear dynamical systems by lifting their behavior into a higher-dimensional space. This article presents a comprehensive review of the main methodologies for estimating the Koopman operator, with particular attention to forced systems–those influenced by external inputs. The approaches are organized into three primary categories: variants of Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD), sparse regression techniques such as Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy), and data-driven methods based on deep neural networks. Building on this foundation, we propose a unified strategy for Koopman operator estimation and its integration into a model predictive control (MPC) framework. Using a multi-tank system as a case study, we show that the Koopman-based MPC yields a response that is twice as fast and significantly more stable under external disturbances–including fault conditions such as leaks–compared to a conventional linearized MPC. These results underscore the Koopman operator’s potential to enhance the modeling, control, and fault diagnosis of complex systems, offering a promising foundation for the development of robust, disturbance-tolerant predictive control architectures.

title: A type-3 fuzzy synchronization system subjected to hysteresis quantizer inputs and unknown dynamics: Applicable to financial and physical chaotic systems
abstract: In this paper, a new control approach is proposed for the synchronization and stabilization of a class of chaotic systems with unknown dynamics and input nonlinearities. Type-3 fuzzy logic systems (T3-FLSs) are developed to adaptively model the dynamics of both master and slave systems in real time. The input is affected by sector-bounded hysteresis and quantization, and these challenges are explicitly addressed in the control design. Unlike conventional methods, the proposed strategy does not require prior knowledge of the system equations or the derivatives of system signals. The adaptation laws for the T3-FLS parameters and estimation errors are rigorously derived using stability and robustness analysis, ensuring smooth control signals without chattering. Extensive simulations and real-time examinations demonstrate that the method achieves accurate synchronization even under severe uncertainties, high levels of random noise, and non-identical chaotic systems. Comparative results confirm the superiority of the proposed approach over existing fuzzy control methods.

title: Multi-objective graph optimization for dynamic task–machine assignment in STEP-NC compliant smart factories using extended Floyd–Warshall algorithm
abstract: Future smart factories equipped with STEP-NC compliant machine tools promise a shift from machine-specific G-code to interoperable and feature-based manufacturing. While this enables unprecedented task assignment flexibility, it introduces a critical challenge in optimally allocating machining tasks across a heterogeneous and dynamic manufacturing floor. This limitation compromises factory resilience which can lead to accelerated resource wear, suboptimal throughput, and poor responsiveness to disruptions such as machine failures. To address this, we formulate the task-to-machine assignment as a multi-objective graph optimization problem. Our solution centers on an extended Floyd–Warshall algorithm that operates in a 4D state space by simultaneously evaluating task sequences, machine capabilities, and spatial constraints. This approach efficiently generates globally optimal manufacturing sequences that are both temporally efficient and physically executable. An empirical Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) surrogate testbed validates the approach by isolating and stress-testing the cyber–physical communication architecture under dynamic physical distress. Disruption scenarios confirmed the system's self-healing capability and demonstrated autonomous recovery from cascading hardware faults with a proven median latency of <1.5 s. Furthermore, 10 ms edge-level safety reflexes successfully protect physical nodes from severe parameter fluctuations, enforcing a “Correct-by-Construction” safety paradigm. Qualitatively, the framework provides factory managers with a highly tunable operational strategy to seamlessly shift between rush order processing and high-precision distributed routing while guaranteeing physical execution. By effectively transforming raw STEP-NC data into operationally feasible schedules that exhibit graceful degradation during disruptions, this work provides a critical step toward resilient and autonomous manufacturing systems capable of self-optimization in the face of dynamic change.

title: Integrating CFD, molecular dynamics, and AI techniques for thermal management of heat transfer devices in microelectronic chip cooling using nano-enhanced PCMs and hybrid cooling systems
abstract: Thermal management plays a key role in ensuring efficient operation across EVs, aerospace, power plants, and high-performance computing. Excessive heat flux and rising operating temperatures can significantly compromise the reliability and efficiency of devices such as CPUs, GPUs, and stretchable electronics. This review addresses thermal stress issues in modern electronic systems and highlights advanced cooling strategies, with a particular focus on microchannel heat exchangers (MCHS). Further this review emphasizes on evaluating cooling technologies for better energy efficiency and clean-energy support, highlighting nanofluids and PCMs for effective transient heat control. This study presents a recent progress in computational approaches including molecular dynamics simulations (MDS), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning techniques such as genetic algorithms and artificial neural networks for optimizing microchannel geometries and enhancing heat transfer efficiency. Special attention is given to emerging microchannel designs, fluid flow behavior, and cooling performance, including concepts such as the Zwieback–Fung effect and fractal like branching channels. The review concludes by outlining future research directions toward the development of highly efficient and cost-effective cooling solutions for next-generation high-power electronic systems.

title: A scenario-driven review of multi-agent cooperation for lunar surface missions
abstract: The transition from short-term lunar sorties to sustained International Lunar Research Station calls for multi-agent cooperative systems. However, terrestrial swarm paradigms face a severe reality gap under lunar constraints in communication, SWaP, and radiation-hardened computing. This systematic review organizes lunar multi-agent research using a new operational taxonomy spanning three mission phases and a six-domain cooperative technical framework, and assesses validation readiness via an Evidence Maturity scale (L0–L4). Our evidence-weighted synthesis shows a bifurcated maturity landscape: while foundational exploration and mapping architectures have achieved L3 validation in terrestrial planetary analogs, actual lunar flight deployments (L4) remain absent, and research into construction, logistics, and maintenance is critically sparse. Our synthesis further reveals that validated systems consistently adopt hybrid modular architectures with communication-aware planning and human-on-the-loop supervision, while fully decentralized end-to-end learning paradigms remain confined to simulation. We further expose an assumption gap between algorithmic prerequisites and lunar physical reality. To narrow the sim-to-real chasm, we identify transferable methods from deep-space learning and in-orbit servicing, and propose a roadmap emphasizing communication autonomy, task self-organization, and engineering realism.

title: Deployment-oriented multi-objective feature selection and neural architecture optimization for comprehensive diesel engine performance prediction
abstract: Comprehensive diesel engine performance prediction, covering power, fuel economy, emissions, thermal state, and combustion response, requires a balance among predictive accuracy, robustness, model compactness, and computational efficiency, which conventional accuracy-driven optimization does not adequately address. This limitation makes it difficult to select suitable models for digital-twin analysis, online estimation, and low-latency deployment. To address this issue, a deployment-oriented multi-objective optimization framework is developed based on Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise and Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III to jointly select input features and optimize heterogeneous neural architectures, including multilayer perceptron (MLP), radial basis function (RBF), and Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN). Six objectives are optimized simultaneously: mean loss, loss variation rate, test-set R(Pitchaiah et al., 2023 2), parameter count, training time, and inference time. KAN delivers the highest predictive fidelity (best test-set R2 = 0.9668) with approximately 2530 parameters and tends to select combustion-process variables, indicating suitability for high-fidelity offline analysis. MLP achieves a balanced accuracy–stability trade-off (best R2 = 0.9177) with control-related variables, supporting stable online estimation. RBF provides the lightest candidate solution, with only 173 parameters and an inference time of 0.00001 s, supporting fast local mapping and latency-sensitive deployment. Overall, no single architecture dominates all objectives; deployment constraints should determine both feature subsets and neural architecture choices for comprehensive diesel engine performance prediction.

title: Universal nonlinear dynamics in damped and driven physical systems: From Pendula via Josephson junctions to power grids
abstract: Understanding the collective behavior of dynamical systems is essential for explaining various emergent phenomena in natural and engineered settings. A key step in this process is formulating an appropriate mathematical description of the individual systems and network of systems. In this context, a range of physical systems is considered here, including the classical pendula, superconducting Josephson junctions, power grids, and various others. Despite the diversity of the systems in terms of physical structure and their application domains, they exhibit strikingly similar dynamical features, namely, phase dynamics governed by inertia and damping, and in their response to external forcing. This observation creates interest and motivates a search for a unified theoretical framework capable of capturing the fundamentals of their dynamical behaviors exhibited across the systems. This review critically examines the up-to-date research activities on the dynamics of the second-order phase oscillator, henceforth claimed here as a universality class by its own merits as a simple nonlinear dynamical model representing a broad class of physical systems. It offers a common mathematical framework to develop a comprehensive understanding, from a general perspective, that bridges, the theoretical and experimental observations of pendulum motion, Josephson junctions, and power grids and their collective behaviors. While each of these systems has been discussed in disparate physical contexts, their underlying mathematical structures reveal strong commonalities. In particular, we highlight the importance of analyzing these systems through the lens of nonlinear phase dynamics to uncover their shared mechanisms and system-specific variety of behaviors as well. This survey mainly focuses on some specific interrelated themes: (i) collective phenomena and emergent synchronization; (ii) the role of heterogeneity in terms of system parameters and effects of noise on the emergent dynamics; (iii) multi-stability and complex transient regimes; (iv) the integration of machine learning for model discovery, control, and prediction; and (v) the broader applicability of phase oscillator models across diverse domains beyond the canonical systems considered here. By systematically comparing the dynamical behaviors of the varied physical systems within a cohesive mathematical framework of second-order phase oscillators, this review seeks for the universal and distinctive features of nonlinear dynamics of the three systems, their collective behaviors such as emergent synchrony, partial synchrony, or chimera states, and specifically explains real-life phenomena, and crowd synchrony that may lead to a collapse of a footbridge and the failure of a power grid. Besides our main emphasis on these systems, brief notes have been added on other systems where this second-order phase model explains their dynamical properties. A broad synthesis on the topic will not only deepen our theoretical understanding but also suggest any design and control of complex dynamical systems in both natural and engineered settings.

title: An integrated risk assessment framework for aircraft systems based on system-theoretic process analysis and fuzzy linguistic consensus decision-making
abstract: As physical and functional interconnections become more complex, aircraft systems require comprehensive risk assessment. However, existing methods still face challenges, leading to inaccurate risk identification and evaluation under epistemic uncertainty. This paper proposes a framework integrating system-theoretic process analysis (STPA) with fuzzy linguistic consensus decision-making. First, we couple STPA with hesitant fuzzy linguistic term set (HFLTS), identifying the latent risk factors, and formalizing the risk factor evaluation problem. Then, the heterogeneous expert evaluations are aggregated through linguistic unification and a joint-optimized fuzzy c-means (FCM) clustering algorithm. Further, the critical risk factors are determined using a reinforcement learning-based hierarchical consensus reaching strategy, enhancing the adaptability of consensus evaluation to complex engineering scenarios, and extending the application of reinforcement learning in risk assessment. The applicability and effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated by the case study of a flight control system. The results show that the proposed framework is robust and significantly improves agreement, with Kendall’s coefficient of concordance increasing from 0.3271 to 0.7547. Compared with existing approaches, the proposed framework achieves more accurate and consistent results, providing practical guidance for risk mitigation in the aviation industry.

title: Modal energy framework for multi-frequency oscillations in renewable grids
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy is accelerating the transition towards renewable-dominated and converter-rich power grids, while also introducing new stability challenges. Among these, multi-frequency oscillations have emerged as a major concern. Spanning frequencies from sub-hertz to kilohertz, arising from interactions among heterogeneous devices, control systems and networks, and evolving under continuously changing operating conditions, these oscillations are challenging to evaluate and mitigate within a unified framework, while also increasing the risk of instability, equipment overstress and maloperation of protection systems. In this Review, we summarize representative oscillation events and the four system-level characteristics of multi-frequency oscillations, assess existing methods for their evaluation and mitigation across different frequency ranges, and discuss the limitations of current approaches in capturing multimode coexistence, mode coupling and time-varying dynamics. Finally, we highlight a unified energy-based perspective as a promising basis for future advances in this field.

title: Chapter 5: Artificial intelligence in cardiac drug delivery vehicles
venue: AI Powered Drug delivery to Neuro and Cardiovascular Systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has begun to permeate the entire continuum of cardiac drug delivery, fusing data-driven molecular design, physiologically faithful simulation, and closed-loop control into therapeutic platforms capable of sensing, deciding, and acting within the dynamic heart. Machine-learning algorithms now screen polymers, lipids, and bioinspired membranes for optimal myocardial targeting; digital twins forecast nanocarrier dispersion across heterogeneous perfusion territories; reinforcement learners embedded in microrobots refine trajectories through pulsatile coronary flows; and responsive hydrogels modulate payload release when electrochemical cues signal ischemic stress. These converging innovations promise precision that static dosing regimens cannot approximate, yet they also expose fault lines: biased datasets threaten inequitable performance, algorithmic opacity complicates clinical trust, and legacy regulations struggle with adaptive software-hardware-pharma hybrids. The chapter dissects each technological stratum, from nanoparticle inverse design to AI-directed robotic actuators, while mapping the regulatory, ethical, and translational terrain that must be navigated before bedside adoption. Evidence from post-2020 trials illustrates tangible gains in anticoagulant titration, arrhythmia-responsive drug release, and risk-tailored stent aftercare, suggesting the first contours of a paradigm where cardiovascular therapy becomes a continuous dialogue between biological signal and computational response. What once resembled speculative fiction, microscale agents repairing myocardium under algorithmic guidance, now rests on demonstrable scientific foundations, pushing the field toward an era in which intelligent cardiotherapeutics are not ancillary aids but intrinsic partners in patient-specific care.

title: Stability of floating offshore wind turbines: A review of mechanisms, control technologies and performance evaluation
abstract: Floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) represent a pivotal technology for harnessing wind energy in deep waters, but their large-scale commercialization remains constrained by complex stability challenges. While significant progress has been made in individual mooring or platform designs, the systematic synthesis of FOWTs stability is still lacking. To bridge this gap, this review provides a comprehensive analysis characterizing FOWTs stability as a systems engineering problem governed by multi-source environmental excitations and nonlinear aero-hydro-servo-elastic couplings. Specifically, the study systematically evaluates the intrinsic stability of major platform configurations and analyzes the evolving role of mooring systems from passive station-keeping to active stability regulation. Crucially, this review consolidates key advances spanning passive structural adaptation and active system-level intelligent control, as well as deterministic analysis and life-cycle reliability assessment. Besides, this review delineates a synergistic framework of artificial intelligence into FOWTs stability research, including reinforcement learning-based intelligent control, multi-fidelity hybrid modeling, and predictive digital models. By integrating these multifaceted perspectives, this study provides an integrated understanding for ensuring the structural integrity and economic viability of FOWTs.

title: Process-intensified multivariate evaluation of long-term thermal efficiency and operational dynamics in circulating fluidized bed boilers
abstract: This research examines the sustained thermal efficiency and operational characteristics of a Circulating Fluidized Bed (CFB) boiler system in an industrial steam production plant. The novelty of this work is the use of long-term industrial data to quantitatively compare linear, exponential, and polynomial regression models, with and without principal component analysis, for simultaneous evaluation of boiler efficiency and heat recovery. Statistical and multivariate modeling techniques were employed to assess the influence of operational parameters, including bed pressure, bed temperature, cyclone temperature, air-fuel ratio, primary and secondary air, and turbine load, on boiler efficiency (Y₁) and heat recovery (Y₂). The findings indicated that AFR, SA, and cyclone temperature were the primary determinants influencing efficiency. Polynomial regression yielded the most precise predictions (R² = 0.891, RMSE = 1.670). The bed temperature was the primary determinant for heat recovery (R² = 0.580), validating the thermodynamical notion that higher combustion temperatures enhance the energy for heat transfer. PCA significantly reduced model complexity while maintaining comparable predictive performance (R² > 0.4). The results demonstrate that combustion variables interact nonlinearly to govern system performance, providing a quantitative basis for reducing energy losses and achieving process intensification through coordinated operational optimization.

title: Adaptive multi-mode underwater acoustic communication: A comprehensive survey from physical modulations to intelligent decision-making
abstract: Adaptive multi-mode Underwater Acoustic Communication (UAC) represents a critical frontier in overcoming the extreme spatiotemporal uncertainty and non-stationarity of the oceanic medium. This survey provides a systemic synthesis of the field’s evolution, transitioning from fundamental waveform elasticity to high-level cognitive autonomy. Driven by the “performance cliffs” and “detection-decoding gaps” empirically exposed in recent in-situ South China Sea trials and the SFI Smart Ocean Dataset for Acoustic Communication (SODAC), we establish the physical imperative for moving beyond static communication regimes. Central to this work is the delineation of a cohesive architectural bridge that links physical-layer execution — such as hybrid carrier modulation and resilient feedback management — with a hierarchical decision-making framework. We categorize this intelligence into a three-tier evolution: deterministic rule-driven heuristics for engineering stability, mathematical optimization for capacity-seeking resource allocation, and data-driven learning for navigating “black-box” environments under stale Channel State Information (CSI). By further exploring cross-layer optimization for end-to-end reliability, this work establishes a comprehensive roadmap that transitions from component-level adaptation to system-wide autonomous intelligence, offering critical insights for the design of resilient next-generation Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs).

title: Tri-driven graph reinforcement learning for dynamic root cause tracing in UF-RO water treatment processes
abstract: The ultrafiltration-reverse osmosis water treatment process is a highly coupled cyber-physical system vulnerable to cascading failures. To overcome the structural opacity, alarm floods, and limited spatial pathfinding of purely data-driven models, this study proposes a physics-data-knowledge tri-driven Graph Neural Network-Reinforcement Learning architecture, tailoring a dynamic sequential diagnostic framework specifically for UF-RO dual-membrane processes. At the data layer, a dual-driven quantification mechanism filters transient noise while preventing adaptive desensitization to progressive membrane fouling. Subsequently, by injecting physical piping layouts and expert rules as hard constraints, a high-fidelity grey-box physically plausible topology is constructed, effectively mitigating the spurious correlations prevalent in black-box methods. Powered by a Graph Attention Network for spatial perception, the Actor-Critic agent is guided by a multi-objective reward function strictly aligned with hydrodynamic propagation and physical attenuation laws. This mechanism compels the agent to execute autonomous, sequential dynamic inference across the constrained network. Validated against a two-year operational dataset from a full-scale 20,000 m3/d industrial plant, the model accurately converges to physical root causes with a 94.2% hit rate and reconstructs hydrodynamic propagation trajectories achieving an 89.7% path similarity. This study analyzes complex operational topologies, establishing a transparent, physically grounded diagnostic framework for smart water facilities.

title: Vehicle drift motion control: A survey of methodologies, challenges, and future directions in the era of intelligent automation
abstract: Vehicle drifting provides a representative paradigm for studying autonomous motion control under extreme dynamic conditions, where vehicle behavior departs substantially from ordinary handling regimes. Understanding and regulating this nonlinear regime is important for high-performance driving and may also inform future active-safety functions beyond conventional stability-control boundaries. This paper reviews the development of vehicle drifting research since the beginning of the 21st century and summarizes autonomous drifting as a coupled system-level engineering problem. The survey first establishes the fundamental prerequisites for drifting and then reviews motion planning methods, including sampling-based, optimization-based, and learning-based strategies. The core of the paper provides a taxonomy of tracking control methods, critically analyzing the evolution from classical model-based approaches to modern learning-based paradigms and emerging hybrid methods that combine physical structure with data-driven adaptation. This survey further summarizes six representative application scenarios and discusses the fidelity and limitations of validation platforms, including simulation, remote-control vehicles, and full-scale vehicles. Finally, this paper synthesizes the remaining challenges and future research directions from the perspectives of system integration, deployment feasibility, safety assurance, and intelligent chassis evolution.

title: Hybrid AI architectures for solar–wind–battery systems: machine-learning control, fuzzy energy management, robust MPC, and automated source-switching hardware
abstract: This study delineates the evolution of hybrid AI architectures for Solar–Wind–Battery (SWB) microgrids from 2010 to 2025, whereby stochastic irradiance and wind, rapid load fluctuations, storage constraints, converter nonlinearities, and switching transients collectively influence reliability, cost, power quality, and emissions. A PRISMA-aligned refinement workflow amalgamates multidisciplinary records and integrates a final synthesis corpus of 142 studies into a stratified “sense–predict–decide–control–validate” framework that links data acquisition, forecasting, supervisory dispatch, constrained control, and embedded execution. Throughout the corpus, advanced spatio-temporal predictors progressively enhance day-ahead and intraday scheduling, while hybrid models integrate learning with traditional control to maintain compatibility with constraints amid domain shifts. Fuzzy and neuro-fuzzy EMS designs remain as interpretable decision frameworks for SOC protection and multi-objective trade-offs in building and microgrid case analyses. Robust Model Predictive Control (MPC) has become the primary safety-focused framework for voltage and frequency control, as well as constraint management, frequently integrated with converter-side Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) and metaheuristic optimisation for multi-timescale coordination. Research focused on hardware indicates an increasing interest in automated source switching, charge-control logic, and protective interlocks; nonetheless, evidence of deployability remains predominantly inside simulations, with a scarcity of EMT/HIL/prototype demonstrations and minimal field reporting. The synthesis produces a validation framework and KPI map—unmet load, curtailment, SOC violations, frequency/voltage excursions, losses, and emissions—facilitating consistent comparisons and a clearer transition from algorithms to implementable SWB controllers. A reporting checklist and an open benchmark suite are advised to enhance reproducibility. The reported KPIs encompass LCOE, unmet load, curtailment, SOC stress, frequency and voltage deviations, and carbon metrics in both grid-connected and islanded modes.

title: Adaptive slip vectoring for speed and yaw-rate control in electric vehicles with four in-wheel motors
abstract: A non model-based control architecture, called adaptive slip vectoring, is presented to regulate speed and yaw-rate in a fully electric vehicle equipped with four in-wheel induction motors. The actuators redundancy is dealt with by a Slip Vectoring strategy which, given a driving force and a driving yaw-moment as control constraints, allocates optimal slip references to each tire, so that four speed references are provided to the four in-wheel motors on the basis of vehicle accelerations, speed and yaw-rate regulation errors. In order to drive independently each in-wheel motor speed to its reference, a decentralized feedback control loop is designed which leads to exponentially convergent load torque estimates so that the torque–slip operating conditions can be monitored online and the load torque requirements are matched for each tire. As a result four decentralized current-pair reference inputs are provided to each motor. Structural sufficient conditions for local exponential stability of the speed and yaw-rate regulation are obtained for uniform rectilinear references. A new overall stability index is introduced and monitored online, and an automatic longitudinal speed reduction can be performed with the goal of keeping such a stability index within a predetermined range so that the structural sufficient conditions are met. Realistic CarSim simulations are presented: (i) a snowy uphill path illustrates the non model-based speed reduction driven by the stability index monitoring; (ii) standard moose-test maneuvers on dry and wet asphalt illustrate uniform yaw-rate tracking performance due to the continuous differential actions of the four in-wheel torques.

title: From aerial transportation to aerial interaction: A review

BaTiO<ce:inf loc=post>3</ce:inf>:Nd<ce:sup loc=post>3+</ce:sup> nanoparticles: Gamma induced dosimetry properties, optical thermometry and minutia detection using <ce:italic>YOLOv8x</ce:italic> deep learning model
abstract: A series of un-doped and 1–11 mol % of Nd3+ doped BaTiO3 (BTO:Nd3+) nanoparticles (NPs) are synthesized using the solvothermal method. When excited at 808 nm, the NPs emitted near-infrared light (NIR) with four distinct bands linked to Nd3+ transitions: from 4F3/2 to 4I9/2, 4I11/2, and 4I13/2, and from 4F5/2 to 4I11/2. The NPs potential as optical temperature sensors are assessed by measuring the fluorescence intensity ratio (FIR) between coupled and non-coupled levels over a temperature range of 303–463 K. This led to two FIR-based sensing methods: one using the 868 nm emission (4F3/2 to 4I9/2) and the other using the 948 nm emission (4F5/2 to 4I11/2). The FIR of these emissions is investigated as a function of temperature within the range of 303–463 K. For the emission at 868 nm, the maximum absolute sensitivity is 0.00152 K−1, the relative sensitivity is 0.395 % K−1, and the minimum temperature resolution is 1.4 K. In comparison, for the 948 nm emission, the absolute sensitivity reached 0.00119 K−1, with a relative sensitivity of 1.32 % K−1 and a minimum temperature resolution of 0.84 K. The gamma (γ)-ray irradiated NPs exhibited a thermoluminescence (TL) peak around 120 °C, with the intensity increasing linearly. A computerized glow curve deconvolution algorithm is employed to analyze the complex TL glow curves recorded for the NPs exposed to γ-rays. The 60Co γ-ray (15 kGy) irradiated 7 mol % Nd3+ doped BTO sample exhibited peaks at 119, 162 and 211 °C with the corresponding activation energies (E) 0.088, 0.164 and 0.797 eV. The repeatability and fading signal trends observed in TL experiments provide strong evidence that BTO:7Nd3+ NPs are suitable for dosimetry applications, showing consistent and reliable results. These findings also suggest that the NPs effectively measure dose-related changes. Additionally, this study examines the application of powder dusting for fingerprint (FP) detection across various substrates, focusing on the visualization of Level I-III features and ensuring long-term stability of developed FPs. The findings highlight the technique's reliability for forensic investigations, offering durable and detailed FP impressions. This study applies You Only Look Once version 8x (YOLOv8x), a cutting-edge deep learning model, for accurate, real-time detection of latent fingerprints (LFPs) in forensic investigations. In summary, BTO:Nd3+ NPs is highly promising for optical thermometry and LFP detection due to its exceptional sensitivity, precise temperature resolution, and effective luminescence.

title: A comprehensive review of AI-driven approaches for smart grid stability and reliability
abstract: The stability and reliability of smart grids are essential for ensuring efficient and secure electricity delivery, particularly amid the increasing integration of renewable energy sources. This review presents a comprehensive analysis of artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods for real-time grid management, and fault detection. Unlike previous works that focus on isolated grid functions, this study provides a unified framework encompassing energy monitoring and control, optimization, and resilience. Machine learning, deep learning, and reinforcement learning techniques are systematically evaluated across diverse grid tasks, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and implementation challenges. Special attention is given to hybrid models that combine AI with optimization strategies to address issues such as scalability, computational complexity, and adaptability. The paper identifies critical research gaps and offers actionable recommendations to advance AI-driven smart grid operations, promoting more resilient, adaptive, and intelligent power systems.

title: Synchronization control for optical micromanipulation of cell ensembles with shape constraints
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: Precise control of cell ensembles is essential for applications requiring maintenance of collective geometric configuration, such as tissue morphogenesis and cell-based microrobotics. This study proposes a novel optical manipulation framework that enforces shape-constrained motion of cell groups using synchronized optical tweezers. A time-varying geometric constraint is employed to define the desired shape, while synchronization functions ensure intercellular coordination. A distributed feedback controller is developed, integrating both position tracking errors and coupling-induced synchronization errors, maintain the shape integrity throughout dynamic transitions. Lyapunov-based analysis guarantees asymptotic convergence of both error terms. Simulations demonstrate robust structural consistency during transformations between a rounded rectangle, ellipse, rhombus, and star, with reduced deviations in both position and intercellular alignment compared to non-synchronized methods. The proposed method enables scalable, real-time coordination of cell clusters, providing a foundational step toward programmable tissue engineering and high-precision micromanipulation.

title: Mechano-X coupling in multifunctional mechanical metamaterials
venue: Current Opinion in Solid State and Materials Science
abstract: Mechanical metamaterials emerge as architected materials that derive unprecedented properties from architecture rather than composition. Recently, attention has focused on multifunctional mechanical metamaterials (MMMs) that integrate multiple mechanical and physical functionalities within a single material system. This review presents a Mechano-X coupling overview of recent advances in MMMs. First, four representative architectural intelligences are categorized: lattice-based, origami-inspired, nonlinearity-embedded, and wave-governed MMMs. Deformation mechanisms, load-transfer pathways, and static–dynamic mechanical responses within these architectures collectively generate Mechano-X coupled multifunctionalities. Next, methodological advances for MMMs are reviewed, including topology optimization, machine learning-based prediction and generative artificial intelligence-powered inverse design, that enable demand-driven advancement and exploration. Then Mechano-X coupling paradigm is outlined, distinguishing mechanical–mechanical, mechanical-acoustic/wave, and mechanical-multiphysical couplings that allow simultaneous mechanical performance, wave manipulation, and multiphysical responses. Finally, the challenges and future directions regarding manufacturability, structural toughness, standardization, and sustainability are emphasized. Overall, MMMs represent an architectural intelligence that enables excellent performance, multifunctional integration, and on-demand tunability, thereby offering exceptional promise for advanced and practical engineering applications.

title: A bibliometric mapping study on advances in the operational safety of maglev trains
venue: Journal of Railway Science and Technology

title: Agent technologies in smart manufacturing: A comprehensive review of evolution, architectures, and edge–cloud deployment
abstract: As modern manufacturing systems demand increasing levels of complexity, flexibility, and intelligence, agent-based technologies are emerging as a key paradigm for enabling distributed control, adaptive decision-making, and collaborative autonomy. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the development trajectory and deployment pathways of agent systems in the context of smart manufacturing. Based on temporal evolution, the progression of agents is categorized into three major stages: Traditional Agents, AI Agents, and Agentic AI. To better elucidate the functional roles and technological advancements of various agent types within manufacturing systems, this study proposes a mapping framework grounded in the “cloud–edge–device” collaborative architecture. Four representative agent types are defined accordingly: Reactive Agents, Cooperative Agents, Cognitive Agents, and Agentic AI. Their core capabilities and typical application scenarios are systematically analyzed across different deployment layers. Furthermore, the paper synthesizes current research achievements, identifies critical technical challenges arising from trends such as Industry 5.0, large language models (LLMs), and cross-domain integration, and outlines future research directions. This review aims to provide a structured theoretical reference and a systematic cognitive framework for both research and practical implementation of agent technologies in smart manufacturing, thereby fostering the evolution of manufacturing systems toward greater autonomy, collaboration, and human-centricity.

title: Forging certainty: A novel framework for the specification of combination products
abstract: The specification for a combination product represents a critical covenant of its quality. Too often, the current intellectual framework for forging this covenant remains a fragmented patchwork of legacy pharmaceutical and medical device paradigms. This paper argues that significant product failures are not random accidents but predictable consequences of these historical limitations. We therefore propose a novel, deductive framework—Quality by Design in Specification (QbD-S)—that complements existing empirical methods to address this systemic challenge. This paper presents a formal intellectual engine, the Universal Attribute Generator (UAG), which deconstructs therapeutic failure into five foundational Tenets and uses a rigorous "Interrogatory Filter" (Stress ' Capacity) to systematically derive a comprehensive set of quality attributes. This framework introduces the Criticality Vector to contextualize consequence by adding the dimension of "Context" to the standard scalar of "Severity," and mandates a Structured Falsification Protocol to build scientific confidence in its conclusions. The ultimate output is a "Master Control Strategy"—a binding regulatory mandate that legislates the "Fate" of each attribute, enabling either "Input-Controlled" Real-Time Release or mandating traditional "Symptom-Controlled" testing. QbD-S provides a systematic engine for translating patient needs into a scientifically rigorous and defensible covenant of quality.

title: Advances in machine learning-based active vibration control for automotive seat suspensions: A comprehensive review
abstract: With the rise of intelligent vehicles, the driving and riding experience has undergone significant changes. However, research on intelligent active vibration control of seat suspension systems, which is closely related to ride comfort and safety, remains in its early stages. This paper explores novel machine learning-based control algorithms and their potential applications in active vibration control of seat suspension systems, particularly how the algorithms such as supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning (RL) can overcome the limitations of traditional control methods. Given the lack of comprehensive reviews in this field, this paper aims to provide researchers with a systematic analysis by reviewing machine learning algorithms and their successful applications in other domains and discussing their application potential in active vibration control of seat suspension systems. In doing so, it seeks to offer new insights for the intelligent development of this field.

title: Chapter 5: Integration of edge-enabled IoT in vehicular networks in smart cities
abstract: The integration of edge-enabled IoT into vehicular networks contributes to the fruitful development of ITS in smart cities, improving safety, responsiveness, and efficiency. Edge computing works closely to support real-time decision-making processes that are crucial for the application scenarios mentioned above, such as autonomous driving, traffic optimization, and accident prevention. This method uses the automatic decision-making abilities of machine learning and augmented deep learning methods like convolutional neural networks (CNN) for workload offloading and scheduling. Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication through edge nodes and smart sensors can be enhanced further to achieve an incident-free and smooth interaction between vehicles, infrastructure, and pedestrians for optimizing traffic. It addresses security, data privacy, and scalability issues, and helps build resilient and adaptive vehicular networks. Case studies from worldwide smart city initiatives show how these technologies influence the real world. In terms of latency reduction, the successive authentication method shows a 45% reduction compared to DTTCH and DRL method. When comparing the energy consumption rates, the GA method stands out with 24% relative to methods like ARO, MDP, and ECDSA. This chapter attempts to demonstrate how edge-enabled IoT in-vehicle networks may alter urban transportation and build smarter, more sustainable cities by offering a framework for deploying them.

title: Adverse rotorcraft pilot couplings—Past, present and future challenges
abstract: Fixed and rotary wing pilots alike are familiar with potential instabilities or with annoying limit cycle oscillations that arise from the effort of controlling aircraft with high response actuation systems. Understanding, predicting and suppressing these inadvertent and sustained aircraft oscillations, known as aircraft (rotorcraft)-pilot couplings (A/RPCs) is a challenging problem for the designers. The goal of the present paper is to give an overview on the state-of-the-art in RPC problem, underlining the future challenges in this field. It is shown that, exactly as in the case of fixed wing APCs, RPCs existed from the beginning of rotorcraft development and that the problem of eliminating them is not yet solved: the current rotorcraft modelling for RPC analysis is rather limited to the particular case analysed and there is a lack of quantitative pilot behavioural models to analyse RPCs. The paper underlines the importance of involuntary pilot control actions, generally attributed to biodynamic couplings in predicting RPCs in rotorcraft. It is also shown that recent experiences demonstrate that modern rotorcraft seem to embed tendencies predisposing the flight control system FCS system towards dangerous RPCs. As the level of automation is likely to increase in future designs, extending to smaller aircraft and to different kinds of operation, the consequences of the pilot 'fighting' the FCS system and inducing A/RPCs needs to be eradicated. In Europe, the ARISTOTEL project (2010-2013) has been launched with the aim of understanding and predicting modern aircraft's susceptibility to A/RPC. The present paper gives an overview of future challenges to be solved for RPC-free design and some new solutions herein. © 2013 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Reinforcement learning-based solution for resource management in fog computing: A comprehensive survey
abstract: The rapid growth of context-aware and latency-sensitive Internet of Things (IoT) applications has exposed the limitations of traditional cloud computing in meeting strict latency requirements. To address these challenges, edge computing paradigms, including fog computing, cloudlets, and edge clouds, have emerged. However, managing resources in fog environments remains complex due to dynamic user demands, heterogeneous architectures, and the difficulty of accurately predicting resource availability using tradition algorithms. Reinforcement Learning (RL) is one of the most prominent machine learning techniques in fog environments, capable of learning and interacting with the environment even when minimal information about the parameters is available. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of RL-based approaches for resource management, covering provisioning, placement, scheduling, allocation, offloading, and load balancing. The reviewed works are systematically summarized, highlighting their strengths and limitations. The survey concludes by identifying key research challenges and outlining future directions for advancing RL-based resource management in fog computing.

title: Design of nonlinear fractional malware transmission model in industrial cyber-physical systems with dual infection rates: Machine predictive analysis with nonlinear exogenous neuroarchitectures
Hierarchical reinforcement learning with kill chain-informed multi-objective optimization to enhance resilience in autonomous unmanned swarm
abstract: The resilience of autonomous unmanned swarms (AUS) serves as a cornerstone for guaranteeing continuous mission execution in the face of adversarial interferences. Contemporary methodologies often suffer from limited generalization efficacy and volatile convergence behavior, primarily due to the intricate, high-dimensional, and dynamically evolving landscape of multi-agent systems. In the context of AUS, conventional single-objective reinforcement learning (RL) paradigms amalgamate conflicting objectives into a unified scalar reward, thereby concealing critical trade-offs and undermining the swarm's capacity for adaptive response under adversarial stressors. To transcend these constraints, we propose HRL-KCIMOO, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that synergistically integrates kill chain-informed knowledge pre-training with dynamic multi-objective optimization. A graph attention encoder is pre-trained via contrastive representation learning, graph topology reconstruction, and centrality-aware ranking tasks, endowing each node with embeddings that intrinsically encapsulate causal linkages between adversarial maneuvers and corresponding defensive countermeasures. Subsequently, a high-level actor-critic architecture, augmented with short-term memory through LSTM modules, generates a temporally adaptive weight vector to dynamically reconcile objectives concerning rapid resilience restoration, sustained operational continuity, and long-term systemic robustness. In parallel, decentralized low-level agents execute context-sensitive cooperative behaviors or structural reconfigurations in accordance with the computed objective weights. Comprehensive empirical analyses across diverse adversarial landscapes demonstrate that HRL-KCIMOO consistently surpasses established benchmarks. Notably, even under severe conditions of swarm attrition, the proposed approach sustains significantly superior mission success rates compared to conventional methodologies.

title: Thermal Management Strategies for Electronic Systems
venue: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer

title: Visualization analysis of research trends on thermal runaway warning of lithium-ion batteries: a bibliometric study
abstract: Lithium-ion battery thermal runaway warning (LIBTRW) is critical for ensuring the safety of electric vehicles and energy storage systems. From the Web of Science Core Collection database, this study systematically retrieves 1190 relevant articles published from 2003 to 2025. Using VOSviewer and CiteSpace, this study presents the first bibliometric analysis of LIBTRW research, including the development trends, research patterns, collaboration networks, publication sources, and citation characteristics. Keyword clustering and evolution path analysis are further performed to identify research hotspots and summarize mainstream early warning methods. The results reveal that the field has experienced an explosive growth since 2019. China dominates publication volume, while European and North American countries exhibit higher average citations per article. Tsinghua University and Beijing Institute of Technology are core research institutions. Scholars such as Ouyang MG, Feng XN, and Wang QS constitute the core author group. The Journal of Energy Storage, Journal of Power Sources, and Applied Energy are the primary publication sources. Research hotspots have shifted from early studies on thermal runaway mechanisms and temperature and voltage monitoring toward systematic directions, including multi-parameter fusion warning, gas sensing, and expansion force monitoring. Ten major research clusters are systematically identified, revealing a technological evolution path from mechanism elucidation to fault diagnosis and then to intelligent early warning. Based on these findings, future research should prioritize sensor reliability validation in real-world scenarios, robust deep learning methods with improved generalization, and module-level early warning testing to bridge the gap between academic research and engineering practice.

title: A comprehensive review of adversarial attacks on autonomous driving: From single-modality to multi-sensor fusion
abstract: The safety of Autonomous Vehicles relies heavily on the robust perception in heterogeneous environments; however, vulnerabilities within both physical sensor mechanisms and deep learning algorithms create a critical bottleneck for real-world deployment. Unlike prior surveys restricted to isolated modalities, this paper presents a comprehensive review that rigorously bridges the gap between single-sensor vulnerabilities and multi-sensor fusion fragility. Spanning Camera, LiDAR, Radar, and GPS modalities, we analyze pivotal studies through a novel Task-Centric Taxonomy. Our analysis follows a bottom-up trajectory: we first dissect the fundamental perturbation mechanisms in individual sensors, and then elucidate how these single-modality attacks exploit fusion logic flaws to precipitate system-wide cascading failures, effectively exposing the redundancy paradox in current fusion architectures. To counteract these threats, we systematically categorize contemporary countermeasures into a hierarchical defense framework consisting of model-level immunity, data-level purification, and system-level cross-modal arbitration. Furthermore, we critique the validity gap in evaluation protocols and posit that emerging paradigms, such as End-to-End driving and World Models, inevitably expand the adversarial attack surface. To foster sustainable research, we maintain a continuously updated repository at https://github.com/Lyon2020/MSP-Attacks.

title: Control strategies, schemes, and architectures applied to distribution networks with integration of distributed energy resources
venue: International Journal of Electrical Power & Energy Systems
abstract: AbstractRecent control strategies for power distribution networks increasingly incorporate schemes based on distributed energy resources, prompting questions regarding their roles and impacts within control frameworks. There is a growing need to evaluate the performance of control strategies employing various schemes. Additionally, the potential influence of external factors, such as weather conditions and customer behavior, on the operation of these schemes and overall network performance warrants careful consideration. This paper provides a comprehensive literature review of current control strategies, emphasizing the effects of simultaneous operation of diverse resources and external factors, including weather variability and consumer behavior, on grid performance. The methodology includes systematic categorization of control schemes and multi-level architectures, as well as an examination of emerging data-driven and stochastic modeling approaches. The findings indicate that decentralized control provides the agility required for modern grids, although its effectiveness depends on addressing practical challenges such as communication delays and data quality concerns. The review concludes that advancing control strategies will require not only improved algorithms but also standardized metrics and robust cyber-physical security measures to address the complexity of sustainable energy systems.

title: Control barrier function based visual servoing for Mobile Manipulator Systems under functional limitations
abstract: This paper proposes a new control strategy for Mobile Manipulator Systems (MMSs) that integrates image-based visual servoing (IBVS) to address operational limitations and safety constraints. The proposed approach based on the concept of control barrier functions (CBFs), provides a solution to address various operational challenges including visibility constraints, manipulator joint limits, predefined system velocity bounds, and system dynamic uncertainties. The proposed control strategy is a two-tiered structure, wherein the first level, a CBF-IBVS controller calculates control commands, taking into account the Field of View (FoV) constraints. By leveraging null space techniques, these commands are transposed to the joint-level configuration of the MMS, while considering system operational limits. Subsequently, in the second level, a CBF velocity controller employed for the entire MMS undertakes the tracking of the commands at the joint level, ensuring compliance with the predefined system's velocity limitations as well as the safety of the whole combined system dynamics. The proposed control strategy offers superior transient and steady-state responses and heightened resilience to disturbances and modeling uncertainties. Furthermore, due to its low computational complexity, it can be easily implemented on an onboard computing system, facilitating real-time operation. The proposed strategy's effectiveness is illustrated via simulation outcomes, which reveal enhanced performance and system safety compared to conventional IBVS methods. The results indicate that the proposed approach is effective in addressing the challenging operational limitations and safety constraints of mobile manipulator systems, making it suitable for practical applications.

title: A method for constructing digital twins of production lines based on an object-oriented distributed model-free adaptive algorithm
abstract: With the widespread application of automated production lines in factories, the number and types of production line equipment are numerous, and the operation logic among the equipment is also highly complex. Studying how to accurately construct a digital twin model for automated production lines is of great significance. Currently, most popular digital twin modeling methods are based on sensors and physical models. However, they cannot accurately establish a digital twin model that can describe the production line and the high - quality mapping between the digital twin and the physical model. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a distributed model - independent adaptive algorithm based on object - oriented thinking. This algorithm improves the accuracy of digital twin modeling and realizes the adaptive interaction of physical - virtual data connection and data dynamic update. Based on the object - oriented concept, digital twins are constructed for each production unit of the automated production line. Using multi-sensor collection and fusion technology, multiple-source manufacturing information of the production line is collected as the attributes of each digital twin. On this basis, the problem of consensus tracking control based on data in a multi-agent system with unknown nonlinear dynamic characteristics is further discussed. By applying dynamic linearization technology to each digital twin in the pseudo - partial derivative framework, a distributed model - independent adaptive control algorithm is proposed. This ensures that all digital twins can accurately follow the desired trajectory, thereby achieving real - time intelligent interaction and data synchronization between the digital twins and the physical model. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of this method are verified through a typical forging process. In a typical automated forging production line, under interference conditions, the proposed framework achieves a 44% lower tracking error and a 28% faster response speed than the benchmark scheme based on PID/sensors. Meanwhile, it maintains a stability index of up to 0.98 and reduces the fault condition error rate to 4.8%. The scalability experiment shows that the newly added forging machine can converge to the production rhythm within one production cycle and hardly causes any interference. This indicates strong robustness, scalability, and industrial applicability.

title: Bifurcation-gated kresling origami triboelectric mechanoreceptor enabling self-powered multimodal tactile sensing for intelligent human-robot interaction
abstract: Tactile sensors play major roles in human-robot interaction (HRI) by providing essential feedback on physical stimuli. In this context, bio-inspired design offers a promising route to reproducing the adaptive and multimodal sensing functions of biological tactile systems. Within this biomimetic framework, human-like tactile perception can be achieved by emulating the complementary dual-sensing behaviors of cutaneous mechanoreceptors, comprising Fast-Adaptive (FA) receptors responding to dynamic stimuli, and Slow-Adaptive (SA) receptors producing sustained responses to static stimuli. While triboelectric tactile sensors serve as substantial solutions, their sensing capability is primarily optimized for dynamic motion. In this study, we introduce a bifurcation-gated sensing strategy embodied in a Bio-inspired Origami-based Triboelectric mechanoreceptor (BOT) that discriminates between dynamic and static stimuli through a single compliant structure. The Kresling origami of the BOT exhibits a kinematic bifurcation at a buckling threshold. Below this threshold, dynamic loads produce FA mode, whereas static loads exceeding the threshold activate a SA mode that generates sustained signals during deformation. The BOT achieves highly linear sensing of indentation depth and normal force. Its practical utility is demonstrated through a self-powered collision detection system for safety and a deep learning-based material recognition framework capable of identifying properties under electromagnetic interference (EMI) environments. This work establishes the bifurcation-gated design principle as an alternative to multi-mechanism, opening a pathway toward triboelectric tactile sensors with mechanical property perception for HRI systems.

title: Piezoelectrically actuated control of nonlinear vibrations and resonant instabilities in rotating cylindrical structures
abstract: This research examines how to control axial vibrations using piezoelectric elements and their associated nonlinear vibrational behaviours with regard to rotating cylindrical shells. This will require the use of axial thermal loads in the design model, which utilises the following criteria: (1) As a thin-walled sandwich beam, it consists of a porous functional grading (FG) core and piezoelectric sensor and actuator layers. (2) A thin-walled Rayleigh beam formulation that incorporates geometric nonlinear effects of the von Kármán type to predict varying amplitude of vibration and impact of the piezoelectric elements. (3) The constitutive model of each piezoelectric element, which allows for active control through negative proportional displacement feedback, provides a method for controlling axial vibrations. (4) The governing equations of motion take into account the gyroscopic effects of the rotation and the influence of an interior fluid. The governing equations are derived using Hamilton's principle by retaining all terms up to cubic order and dropping all higher than cubic order terms for the purposes of being analytic. To accomplish this, the Galerkin method is used to convert the resulting partial differential equations (PDEs) into a series of ordinary differential equations (ODEs), and as a group of ODEs, allows the evaluation of a steady state or resonant response using a harmonic trial solution. Investigations into piezoelectric actuation as a means of reducing nonlinear resonant vibrations and preventing dynamic instability from occurring under combined loading conditions that produce thermal, rotational, and fluid loads have been thoroughly conducted. Several parametric analyses reveal how critical rotational speed, thermal gradients, feedback gains, and material gradation are to the conditions that result in the onset of resonant instability and amplitude modulation. The results obtained from these investigations indicate that properly tuned negative displacement proportional feedback can produce a considerable increase in dynamic stability, a reduction in the amplitude of vibration, and a delay of resonance when subjected to multiple types of loading. The results will therefore serve as a useful guideline for designing active vibration control systems for advanced rotating cylindrical systems utilizing multifunctional engineered material architectures.

title: Bridging sensation and actuation: From fundamental architectures to adaptive systems
abstract: Adaptive systems, with their capacity to interact with dynamic environment with self-regulating actions, are driving the development of smart systems across applications ranging from biomedicine and energy to human–machine interfaces. Achieving adaptability requires functional integration between sensors and actuators to transfer from single, fixed operational modes to adaptive behaviors for dynamic scenarios. In this perspective, this review highlights the fundamental mechanisms of tactile sensors and actuators, along with strategies for their functional and performance-level integration. We summarize how adaptive features are embodied in diverse device architectures, revealing distinct characteristics tailored for dynamic functionality at the material and device levels. Furthermore, we focus on application-specific performance enabled by autonomous sensing, regulation, and decision-making. Ultimately, this review outlines key limitations, such as mechanical robustness, dimensional scalability and power management, that need to be overcome to advance adaptive devices from laboratory prototypes to practical, real-world technologies.
