title: Real-Time Vibration-Based Bridge Health Monitoring Systems: A Systematic Literature Review
venue: Iranian Journal of Science and Technology, Transactions of Civil Engineering
abstract: The integrity and reliability of aging bridge infrastructure necessitate advanced monitoring systems capable of real-time anomaly detection. This systematic literature review aimed to assess recent developments in real-time vibration-based structural health monitoring (SHM) technologies. The review employed a structured Scopus search strategy, including predefined keywords, Boolean operators, and eligibility filters, to retrieve relevant literature published from 2015 to 2025. Explicit eligibility criteria were applied, and the identification, screening, eligibility, and inclusion of studies were documented using the PRISMA 2020 flow diagram. Findings highlight substantial progress in sensor technology, particularly smart, energy-autonomous sensors that use triboelectric and piezoelectric energy harvesting and may reduce battery-replacement and maintenance demands. AI-driven methods, including convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, and hybrid statistical techniques, demonstrated promising performance in detecting structural damage and anomalies under varying environmental conditions. Advanced real-time signal processing methods successfully managed computational demands while maintaining data integrity and analytical accuracy. System-level implementations combining finite element updating, edge computing, and decision-support frameworks showed potential to improve structural identification and support more targeted maintenance planning. However, the economic benefits of these systems were not consistently quantified across the reviewed studies and remain dependent on installation, operation, maintenance, communication, intervention, and failure-related cost assumptions. This comprehensive evaluation therefore underscores the potential of integrated SHM systems to enhance bridge safety and operational efficiency while highlighting the need for more rigorous and comparable life-cycle cost evaluations. This review contributes to the theoretical understanding and practical implementation of SHM and identifies future research priorities in computational optimization, transfer learning, standardization, and cybersecurity.

title: Multi-sensor data-driven intelligent product interaction fault self-diagnosis system
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis is crucial for the safety and reliability of dynamic smart manufacturing systems. Existing single-sensor approaches do not model complex, multi-dimensional interactions between robotic components during dynamic interactions. This paper introduces a Kronecker Fused Variational-Evolutionary Reconstruction Framework for Adaptive Intelligent Diagnostics (KROVER-AID), which enables real-time, cross-sensor, and across-sensor fault diagnosis. The Kronecker fusion method captures the high-order cross-dependencies among vibration, current and torque signals to generate unified and discriminative feature embeddings. UNVAE (Unified Nested Variational Autoencoder) serves as a nested encoder-decoder to uncover latent fault features and accurately reconstruct fused representations, thus exposing subtle faults. UNVAE is trained by ERM (Evolutionary Reconstruction Model) using adaptive evolutionary optimization to fine-tune the parameters of the decoder, thus reducing the reconstruction error and improving the adaptability to unseen fault cases. Experimental validation on industrial-scale electric motor datasets with variable load and speed conditions shows that KROVER-AID outperforms the benchmark approaches by 6.5% in fault detection accuracy and 5.8% in F1-score. The proposed framework has demonstrated significant robustness, cross-domain generalization, and autonomous adaptability; therefore, it is a scalable and intelligent approach to predictive maintenance and fault management in next-generation smart manufacturing systems.

title: Lightweight multimodal adaptive swin transformer with normal feature protection for variable-load fault diagnosis
abstract: Addressing feature distribution shifts in variable-load bearing fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a lightweight framework integrating Normal Feature Protection Enhancement (NFPE) and a Multimodal Adaptive Swin Transformer for distributed high-performance industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) monitoring. Unlike traditional augmentation strategies that neglect physical consistency, NFPE explicitly constrains the transformation boundaries of normal samples to maintain a stable detection baseline. A time-frequency dual-stream architecture is constructed to extract complementary features from vibration impulses and thermal characteristics, while a load-aware embedding module dynamically aligns feature spaces across different operating conditions. Benefiting from the window-based self-attention mechanism with linear computational complexity, the proposed architecture exhibits inherent parallel processing capability and is highly compatible with modern heterogeneous computing platforms. Experiments on the KAIST dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 99.15% accuracy in mixed-load scenarios, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art baselines like iTransformer and PatchTST. With only 0.26 M parameters and 0.01 GFLOPs, the model enables sub-millisecond-level real-time inference on edge nodes, effectively reducing the data transmission pressure and computational burden on centralized high-performance computing (HPC) clusters in distributed monitoring systems. This work provides a practical and effective algorithmic solution for building hierarchical industrial health monitoring systems.

title: Physics-driven invertible architecture for unified forward-inverse modeling of magnetorheological dampers
abstract: High-fidelity forward force prediction and inverse current deduction are crucial for the semi-active vibration control of magnetorheological (MR) dampers. However, existing models suffer from bottlenecks like inadequate accuracy, intractable inverse solving, and a lack of physical interpretability. Therefore, this paper proposes a physics-driven invertible architecture (PDIA) for unified forward-inverse MR damper modeling. Unlike physics-informed neural networks relying on soft penalties, PDIA embeds physical mechanisms into the network topology as mandatory hard constraints. Specifically, complex damping dynamics are decoupled into a base response bias, a state modulation factor, and an electromagnetic mapping core, each subjected to targeted physical constraints. The core mapping is mathematically restricted to a global monotonic bijection, and a robust division operator is introduced to guarantee the absolute uniqueness and numerical stability of the inverse solution. Furthermore, a latent space alignment strategy formulates a joint loss within a differentiable domain, circumventing gradient truncation obstacles from discrete root-finding and enabling stable end-to-end joint optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate PDIA’s superior bi-directional performance. In zero-shot generalization tests, its forward and inverse MAE are as low as 0.0170 kN and 0.0211 A. Compared with other models, the PDIA exhibits significant advantages in accuracy, generalization, and stability. Moreover, hardware force-tracking experiments validate its precise tracking of dynamic target commands and practical feasibility. In summary, the proposed architecture mitigates the unconstrained limitations of purely black-box representations in non-linear modeling, offering a robust approach for the bidirectional modeling of magnetorheological dampers.

title: Incremental Graph Construction Enables Robust Spectral Clustering of Texts
abstract: Neighborhood graphs over document embeddings are a common component of text-mining pipelines, supporting topic discovery, deduplication, semi-supervised label propagation, and retrieval-index construction, and they are a critical but fragile step in spectral clustering of text embeddings. On realistic text datasets, standard k -NN graphs can contain many disconnected components at practical sparsity levels (small k ), making spectral clustering degenerate and sensitive to hyperparameters. We introduce an incremental k -NN graph construction algorithm in which each new node is linked to its k nearest previously inserted nodes; this guarantees a connected graph for any k . We provide an inductive proof of connectedness and discuss implications for incremental updates when new documents arrive. We validate the approach on spectral clustering of SentenceTransformer embeddings using Laplacian eigenmaps across eleven sentence- and paragraph-level clustering tasks drawn from six dataset sources in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. Compared to standard k -NN graphs, our method outperforms in the low- k regime where disconnected components are prevalent, and matches standard k -NN at larger k . The advantage at low k persists when the standard k -NN graph is repaired with a minimum spanning tree, while our construction avoids the dense distance matrix an exact repair requires and is consequently far cheaper to build, in both time and memory. The code is available on https://github.com/bkolosk1/incremental_clustering_graphs.

title: Towards explainable anomaly detection for satellite telemetry
abstract: The increasing complexity of modern satellites and the growing amount of telemetry data available pose significant challenges for a safe and economic operation of satellites. To support the satellite engineers, traditional machine learning methods, including deep learning-based approaches, have shown promising results but lack intuitive explainability, hindering their adoption in operational settings. This paper presents a novel approach to anomaly detection and causal inference in satellite telemetry data, leveraging an ensemble of classical statistical models and deep learning architectures, combined with causal discovery techniques. We employ the Peter and Clark momentary conditional independence algorithm for identifying causal relationships with temporal dependencies and use its results as part of an in-depth root cause analysis enhancing anomaly detection. Our approach identifies potential anomalies and provides indications which satellite components cause the detected anomalies in order to facilitate interpretation by satellite operators. By integrating causal inference methods into anomaly detection pipelines, we aim to enhance explainability and facilitate decision-making in complex systems. This paper contributes to the growing body of work on anomaly detection and causal inference, highlighting the potential of combining machine learning and causation for improved operational performance.

title: Measured multi-source fusion graph neural network for semi-supervised imbalanced working condition recognition
abstract: In real-world sucker-rod pumping operations, the acquired condition data typically exhibits a highly imbalanced distribution. Addressing this imbalance through deep learning and graph neural networks, utilizing multiple measured data sources, presents new opportunities for accurate and practical condition recognition. Influenced by the limitations of traditional single-source or multi-source working condition recognition technologies, the extensive requirement for labeled working condition data, and the high robustness demand for identifying actual imbalanced working condition data, existing deep learning-based working condition recognition technologies urgently require improvement in both accuracy and engineering applicability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a semi-supervised, imbalanced working condition recognition method for sucker-rod pumping wells based on measured multi-source data fusion the graph neural network. Specifically, the method first converts the measured dynamometer cards and electrical power cards into graph data using the histogram of oriented gradient and nearest neighbor algorithms, enhancing the feature representation capability of the original working condition data for complex nonlinear systems. Then, graph convolutional networks are employed to extract deeper features from different information sources using a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a feedforward neural network. Based on the consistency constraint, feature representations of each information source are adaptively fused through dynamic learning with the Squeeze-and-Excitation attention mechanism. Next, a focal loss function is introduced to dynamically adjust the sample weights of different categories in the long-tail distribution data. This optimization of the model’s handling of imbalanced data improves its robustness. Finally, the multi-source fused feature representations are incorporated into a graph neural network based on enhanced label propagation, where a logistic regression classifier further explores the potential relationships between a small number of labeled samples and a large number of unlabeled samples, thus enhancing the semi-supervised classification performance of the working condition recognition model. The experimental data were sourced from a high-pressure, low-permeability, thin oil reservoir block in a certain oil field in China. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method effectively integrates multiple measured information sources from sucker-rod pumping wells, a small amount of labeled working condition data, and a large amount of unlabeled working condition data, achieving competitive and stable working condition recognition performance under the evaluated imbalanced scenarios.

title: Explainable LLM-assisted fault diagnosis for smart manufacturing using multi-trace diagnostic rationales and verification
venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
abstract: Smart manufacturing systems increasingly rely on data-driven fault diagnosis to support condition monitoring, predictive maintenance, and operational decision-making. Although conventional machine-learning and deep-learning models can achieve high diagnostic accuracy, their predictions are often difficult for engineers to interpret, verify, or confidently use under uncertain operating conditions. This study presents CoT-FD6, an LLM-assisted diagnostic framework combining standardized sensor features, training-only analogical retrieval, multiple explicit structured diagnostic rationales, modal LLM diagnosis aggregation, independent prototype verification, and selective acceptance or human-review escalation. The framework is evaluated on controlled synthetic manufacturing faults and the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 degradation benchmark, with conventional classifiers tested on the same held-out instances. On the synthetic task, the raw LLM diagnosis achieved $$0.998 \pm 0.004$$ accuracy and macro-F1. On NASA FD001, Logistic Regression, SVM-RBF, and Random Forest achieved accuracies of 0.920, 0.920, and 0.930, respectively, whereas the raw LLM achieved $$0.618 \pm 0.018$$ . Retrieval-only classification reached 0.860 accuracy and the independent verifier 0.910. Selective governance increased accuracy to $$0.900 \pm 0.008$$ among automatically accepted NASA cases at $$0.660 \pm 0.020$$ coverage while capturing $$82.7\%$$ of raw LLM errors. Generated rationales were strongly grounded in the supplied measurements, with grounding rates of 0.982 and 0.995 on the synthetic and NASA datasets, respectively. These results position CoT-FD6 as a complementary explanation, verification, and selective-governance layer rather than a replacement for high-performing supervised fault classifiers.

title: AI-based multivariate analysis of environmental radiation dose trends in Taiwan
venue: Journal of Radioanalytical and Nuclear Chemistry
abstract: Nuclear energy is considered a key low-carbon energy source for sustainable development; however, the potential risks of nuclear accidents necessitate effective environmental radiation dose monitoring. This study integrates radiation dose rate and precipitation data from 63 monitoring stations across Taiwan, incorporating spatial relationships among stations. A Variational Autoencoder architecture was employed to predict site-specific radiation dose rates using approximately 300 consecutive days of time-series data from 2024. Based on radiation observations from the preceding 10 min, the model achieved a mean absolute error below 0.0005 (μSv/h) for 7-min-ahead predictions. The results demonstrate strong predictive performance, while also indicating sensitivity to low radiation thresholds, which may induce periodic oscillations and increase prediction errors.

title: Measurement-Driven Low-Label Adaptation for Signal-Based Areal Surface Roughness Prediction After Tool Replacement in Ti–6Al–4V Milling
abstract: In precision milling, areal surface roughness ( $$S_{\textrm{a}}$$ S a ) is commonly verified through offline surface topography measurement. However, tool replacement can change process signals and reduce the reliability of signal-based $$S_{\textrm{a}}$$ S a prediction. This study formulates $$S_{\textrm{a}}$$ S a prediction in Ti–6Al–4V milling as a measurement-driven low-label target-tool adaptation problem. Three tools were machined under fixed cutting parameters, and each steady-state pass was paired with one confocal white-light $$S_{\textrm{a}}$$ S a measurement. Force and vibration signals were organized using a one-pass–one-sample strategy to avoid overlapping window sample inflation. Seventy-two statistical descriptors were extracted to describe amplitude, energy, fluctuation, distribution, and spectral response characteristics. Descriptor-based regressors and a hierarchical signal statistical fusion model were evaluated using the same leave-one-tool-out (LOTO) protocol. Unlabeled target-tool descriptors were used for per-tool input normalization, and limited target-tool $$S_{\textrm{a}}$$ S a labels were used only for affine output calibration. Raw cross-tool prediction remained unreliable for all models, with negative average $$R^2$$ R 2 values. After calibration, random forest achieved the best numerically calibrated performance in the present controlled setting, with average RMSE/ $$R^2$$ R 2 values of 0.0925 µm/0.4658, 0.0956 µm/0.3331, and 0.0973 µm/0.2908 under pass-uniform calibration, layer-all-pass calibration, and layer-one-pass calibration, respectively. Under the present controlled three-tool LOTO setting, the results indicate that reliable statistical descriptors, unsupervised input alignment, and few-shot affine correction provide a practical route for improving $$S_{\textrm{a}}$$ S a prediction after tool replacement. 1. Tool replacement causes severe $$S_{\textrm{a}}$$ S a prediction bias despite fixed cutting parameters. 2. One-pass samples link steady-state signals with measured $$S_{\textrm{a}}$$ S a values. 3. Few-shot affine calibration improves cross-tool $$S_{\textrm{a}}$$ S a prediction with limited labels.

title: Classifier chains for multi-label learning: a systematic review and taxonomy
abstract: Classifier chains (CC) have become one of the most influential paradigms for multi-label classification since their introduction in 2009. By chaining binary classifiers so that each exploits predictions of its predecessors as additional features, CC offer a principled yet practical mechanism for modeling label dependencies. Despite sustained research interest—with over 200 published works—a systematic-review treatment of this literature has not previously been published. This paper presents a PRISMA-compliant systematic review of classifier chains covering 2009–2026, complementing the perspectives article of Read et al. (JAIR, 2021 ) and the inference-method survey of Mena et al. ( 2016 ). The review is organized around four research questions covering the design space of CC variants, their empirical comparison under a common protocol, their theoretical properties (error propagation, optimality of greedy inference, role of chain order), and the most promising research frontiers. We propose a three-axis taxonomy that organizes CC variants along dependency modeling , inference strategy , and computational profile , and reorganize the analytical review along the algorithmic dimensions of chain order, ensemble strategy, chain structure, and base-classifier learning. Concretely, we contribute (i) a computational-complexity comparison of 18 CC variants, (ii) original reproducible experiments on nine datasets with eight metrics and Wilcoxon signed-rank statistical-significance testing, (iii) a formal treatment of error propagation and a summary of theoretical results on CC, (iv) a discussion of CC for cross-paradigm problems (multi-output regression, multi-dimensional classification, positive–unlabelled multi-label), (v) a source-code availability inventory, and (vi) an analysis of 23 application domains. We discuss seven research directions including integration with large language models, extreme multi-label scalability, and fairness-aware chain construction, and we state the scope limitations of this review explicitly.

title: A novel DGA in oil fault diagnosis model based on improved FCM-SVM for transformer
abstract: To improve the reliability of dissolved gas analysis (DGA) in transformer fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a hybrid diagnosis framework that combines kernel principal component analysis (KPCA), entropy weight-enhanced fuzzy c-means (FCM), and support vector machine (SVM). KPCA is first used to extract a reduced set of gas ratio features, so that the main diagnostic information can be retained while redundant feature components are suppressed. An entropy weight-based adaptive scheme is then introduced into the FCM objective function to reflect the different contributions of individual features during clustering. Based on this design, the clustering stage is further employed to identify ambiguous samples before classification, thereby improving the quality of the samples used for subsequent diagnosis. The retained samples are finally classified by an optimized SVM, whose kernel type and hyperparameters are determined through grid search with cross-validation. The proposed method was evaluated using 630 sets of real transformers DGA data collected from substations. Results show that the proposed model achieved an accuracy of 95.87% on the internal test set, which was higher than those of the modified three-ratio method (85.71%) and the Duval triangle method (76.82%). The ablation results further verified the effectiveness of each component in the proposed framework, while McNemar’s test confirmed that the performance improvement was statistically significant. In addition, external validation on an independent regional dataset produced an accuracy of 96%, suggesting that the proposed model maintains good diagnostic performance under cross-regional data variation. These results indicate that the proposed KPCA-improved FCM-SVM framework can effectively reduce diagnostic ambiguity and improve the accuracy and robustness of transformer fault diagnosis.

title: Agentic AI-driven IPv6 route lookup: a deterministic approach for low-altitude economy networks
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI)-driven low-altitude economy (LAE) networks require high forwarding throughput together with controlled route-update overhead. Large unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms may concentrate longest-prefix-match (LPM) queries at a small number of operationally common IPv6 prefix lengths, particularly /48 aggregation and /64 subnet prefixes. This paper proposes a distribution-aware heuristic binary search (HBS) scheme that uses empirical prefix-length probabilities and entropy to construct an asymmetric search structure. Marker projection and precomputed heuristic search paths (HSPs) preserve LPM correctness without lookup backtracking, while an associated marker list (AML) localizes the marker dependencies affected by route changes. A sliding-window mechanism rebalances the structure when persistent workload changes satisfy the configured triggers. In the evaluated Linux-server benchmark with four forwarding information base datasets and a Zipfian workload, HBS reaches 29.2 million lookups per second (MLPS) on the Cloud dataset and has an average update latency of 0.44 $$\mu \textrm{s}$$ across the four datasets; the corresponding Poptrie and Splitting Approach to Internet Protocol Lookup (SAIL) averages are 11.6 and 4.1 $$\mu \textrm{s}$$ . These measurements demonstrate favorable average performance under the evaluated configuration.

title: Intelligent phase change material envelopes for adaptive and predictive energy storage in smart buildings
abstract: Phase change materials (PCMs) can substantially reduce building energy demand through latent thermal energy storage, but conventional systems are constrained by passive operation and limited adaptability to varying climate, occupancy, and grid conditions. This field has been driven forward by recent advances in adaptive PCMs, predictive control, artificial intelligence, and digital twins, but the existing reviews cover these developments separately. This review summarizes 102 studies published from 2003 to 2026 and proposes a unified three-pillar framework of Hardware Intelligence, Control Intelligence and Data Intelligence for intelligent PCM building envelopes. It is demonstrated that passive PCM systems are inherently constrained by seasonal mismatch, and experimentally confirmed energy savings are on the order of 10–25%. However, with the integration of adaptive hardware and predictive control, reductions in operating cost of 20–57% and peak load shifting of up to 80% are possible. Emerging techniques such as reinforcement learning and differentiable predictive control provide improved adaptability but need more substantial experimental validation. The review concludes that the performance of intelligent PCM depends on the coordinated integration of material, control and data, rather than on isolated technological advances. Integrated material-control co-design, physics-informed artificial intelligence, digital twins and standardized evaluation frameworks are the critical priorities to accelerate grid-interactive, low-carbon building envelopes.

title: What is Attention Mechanism? A Comprehensive Survey of Attention Methods and Transformer Models
abstract: The attention mechanism is a fundamental component widely used in deep learning models across numerous domains and tasks. It enables models to selectively focus on the most relevant parts of the input, rather than processing all elements equally, by assigning weights according to their importance for the task. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the attention mechanism, outlining its general framework and offering a taxonomy of attention models, including Hierarchical, Bidirectional, Multi-Head, Multi-query, Group-query, Graph, Channel, Spatial, Channel-Spatial, Temporal, Spatial–Temporal, Cross, Axial and Flash Attention. The computational trade-offs of these models are also analyzed, and new developments in efficient attention are highlighted. We also discuss the Transformer architecture, one of the most influential deep learning frameworks that makes effective use of attention mechanism and review its major variants including BERT, GPT, Transformer XL, XLNet, BART, Fast Transformer, T5, Longformer, BIGBIRD, Performer, Linformer, Reformer, RoFormer, ALiBi, Switch Transformer, LLaMA, ViT, DETR, DeepViT, DeiT, T2T ViT, CrossViT, PVT, Swin Transformer, TNT, MViT, ViViT, DAT, and Spiking Transformer. Additionally, we provide a comparative overview of these models, highlighting their key ideas, results, advantages, and limitations. Through this survey, we emphasized the pivotal role of attention-based models, especially those built on the Transformer architecture, in shaping diverse application domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and sensor data analysis.

title: Application of artificial intelligence in local dry underwater welding: a review
abstract: Local dry underwater welding (LDUW) creates a localized gas cavity to improve weldability without a full dry habitat, but the cavity remains dynamically coupled to pressurized water. Consequently, pressure, cavity behavior, and sensing-path changes can alter both the welding process and its measured representation, making direct transfer of terrestrial welding artificial intelligence (AI) unreliable. This review critically evaluates existing AI-enabled welding, underwater sensing, robotic perception, defect monitoring, digital-twin, and closed-loop control studies from the perspective of LDUW transferability. Across these studies, two distinct failure mechanisms emerge. Measurement degradation reduces the fidelity, consistency, synchronization, or availability of observations, whereas mechanism shift alters the relationships among process parameters, physical states, sensor responses, and weld quality. The evidence further indicates that visual and geometric sensing provide the strongest spatial basis for localization and observable surface abnormalities, while acoustic and electrical signals more reliably support process-state recognition and defect-risk assessment than confirmed defect identification. Multimodal fusion can reduce ambiguity only when participating measurements remain physically corresponding and individually trustworthy. Overall, current evidence is substantially stronger for isolated sensing, modeling, reconstruction, and control functions than for cross-condition generalization or integrated autonomous LDUW. Future progress therefore depends on pressure- and cavity-aware modeling, reliability-aware multimodal sensing, condition-separated validation, and staged closed-loop control whose authority is constrained by observation and model validity.

title: Current state of research and future developments of artificial intelligence in pain diagnosis and treatment
abstract: Chronic pain represents a significant global health challenge, with traditional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches facing limitations in objective assessment and precision treatment. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technology have opened new avenues for addressing these challenges. This review systematically examines the current state and future trends of AI research in the field of pain medicine. The article focuses on three core research directions: In pain assessment, studies concentrate on leveraging AI to fuse multimodal data (such as facial expressions, voice, and physiological signals) to explore its ability to objectively quantify pain states. In image analysis, various deep learning models have been developed to automatically segment key structures like the spine, nerves, and needle tips from medical images, aiming to enhance identification accuracy and efficiency. In disease management, current research explores AI’s potential value in classification, treatment decision-making, and prognosis prediction for various painful conditions including shoulder joint disorders, osteoarthritis, trigeminal neuralgia, postherpetic neuralgia, and cancer pain. The article concludes with a critical analysis of challenges in this field—including research data generalization, multimodal fusion strategies, model interpretability, and ethical compliance—while outlining future research directions.

title: Introduction to Building Digital Twins
venue: Digital Twins for Building Optimization: Enhancing Energy and Comfort
abstract: This chapter introduces the concept of the Building Digital Twin (BDT) as the natural evolution of modern Building Energy Management Systems (BEMS) and Control System Engineering. It establishes the foundational bridge from Demand-Side Management (DSM) and supervisory automation toward intelligent, data-driven, and continuously synchronized cyber-physical building systems. Beginning with the principles of feedback, prediction, and adaptation, the chapter explains how classical control theory—through both model-based and model-free paradigms—underpins the operational intelligence of Digital Twins. Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) are examined as complementary approaches, each offering unique advantages for handling the slow, nonlinear, and stochastic dynamics which characterize buildings. The chapter distinguishes simulation models from Digital Twins by emphasizing real-time synchronization, closed-loop intelligence, and continuous parameter calibration. Through multi-layered architectures, including perception, virtual modeling, and physical execution, it illustrates how Digital Twins integrate sensing, forecasting, optimization, and learning to support predictive and autonomous building operation. A contrast with fast, deterministic electromechanical systems—exemplified through a motor Digital Twin—highlights the additional complexity and long-memory behavior inherent in building environments. Toward the end, we provide an integrated overview of the challenges, advantages, and new considerations involved in putting BDTs into practical use. Key challenges include nonlinear dynamics, stochasticity, partial observability, model drift, data quality issues, multi-objective trade-offs, and computational burden. These challenges simultaneously justify the need for Computational Intelligence (CI) techniques—surrogate modeling, evolutionary optimization, Reinforcement Learning, and hybrid predictive-learning frameworks—which form the focus of Part II of the book. Ultimately, the chapter positions Digital Twins as predictive, adaptive, and control-oriented constructs which unify physics-based modeling with data-driven intelligence to achieve the next generation of autonomous, grid-interactive, and resilient building operation.

title: Foundations of Computational Intelligence (CI) for Building Digital Twins
venue: Digital Twins for Building Optimization: Enhancing Energy and Comfort
abstract: This chapter establishes Computational Intelligence (CI) as the conceptual bridge between physics-based building simulation and the emerging paradigm of Building Digital Twins (BDTs). Building energy systems are shown to exhibit nonlinear, stochastic, and multi-objective behavior, rendering classical optimization and control approaches insufficient in isolation. Through an illustration of complex search landscapes, global versus local optimization behavior, and Pareto-based trade-offs, optimization is reframed as a process of structured exploration under uncertainty rather than the pursuit of a single optimal solution. The chapter clarifies how CI complements physics-based models by enabling adaptive search, learning, and multi-objective reasoning, thereby addressing fundamental challenges associated with Digital Twin development. Rather than implementing BDTs directly, this chapter prepares the analytical and conceptual foundations upon which subsequent chapters build, motivating the CI methodologies, simulation infrastructures, and surrogate-assisted optimization frameworks developed in the rest of this book.

title: From Entropy to Decommissioning: Cryptographic Key Management Strategies Across the Automotive Supply Chain
venue: Systems, Software and Services Process Improvement and Innovation
abstract: Automotive embedded systems present key management challenges that are qualitatively different from enterprise IT. A vehicle’s cryptographic architecture must support a heterogeneous population of Electronic Control Units—from SHE-equipped body controllers to HSM-rich domain gateways—across a 15–25-year operational lifetime, through a supply chain where trust is contractually negotiated rather than architecturally guaranteed. This paper consolidates the full cryptographic key lifecycle into five logical phases, each examined through its alignment strategies between OEMs, Tier 1 integrators, and Tier 2 silicon vendors, alongside the residual risks that persist regardless of strategy choice. The framework draws on NIST SP 800–57, ISO/SAE 21434, UNECE R155, and practical deployment experience in volume automotive production. The paper further analyzes cross‑phase dependency effects, showing how early lifecycle decisions constrain or amplify residual risk in downstream phases over the vehicle’s operational lifetime.

title: Two-Layer Adaptive Fault Tolerance Framework for Internet of Medical Things: A Weighted Autoencoder with Reinforcement Learning-Based Threshold Adaptation
abstract: Fault tolerance in Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems is challenging due to heterogeneous architectures, stringent safety requirements, and concurrent exposure to cyberattacks and performance degradation. This paper proposes a two-layer adaptive fault tolerance framework integrating lightweight intrusion detection with domain-aware anomaly quantification. The first layer employs a machine learning-based intrusion detection system to produce a binary safety score. The second layer uses a domain-weighted autoencoder to compute a continuous Health Index (HI) from Quality-of-Service metrics and the safety score. The principal contribution is the systematic demonstration that feature weighting within the reconstruction loss plays a central role in safety-critical detection, improving Critical Recall from 7.3% (uniform weighting) to 100% (safety-first weighting) on the evaluated dataset. Decision thresholds are optimized via an $$\epsilon $$ ϵ -greedy Q-learning agent, and a Teacher–Student knowledge distillation pipeline compresses cloud-level intelligence for edge deployment, achieving a $$34.6\times $$ 34.6 × reduction in computational cost while preserving Critical Recall. Experiments on the WUSTL-EHMS-2020 dataset validate the framework against ablation baselines and a structurally comparable state-of-the-art method.

title: Five Measures to Counter Obscure Hazardous Failure Conditions in Foundation Model Systems: A Practical Guide for Safety Engineers
abstract: Machine learning models for natural language processing have achieved remarkable performance across many domains, yet their adoption in safety engineering remains limited. A key barrier are hazardous failure conditions - such as hallucinations - which arise from an insufficient functionality of a foundation model system and must be controlled in safety-critical contexts. This article examines such behavior through a safety lens and traces root causes for obscure hazardous failure conditions in generic foundation model setups. From this analysis, we distill five broadly applicable concepts that provide a structured way to counter these challenges (narrow domain, setup diligence, uncertainty estimation and interpretability, iterative approaches, hybrid approaches). Together, they offer a principled starting point for deriving concrete design and assessment practices for safety engineers working with language-model-based systems. We illustrate our approach through three representative use cases that demonstrate how these five countermeasures can be applied in real-world safety engineering scenarios.

title: Eva Optimizer: Escaping Low-Curvature Traps in Deep Learning
abstract: Adaptive optimization methods like Adam excel in handling sparse gradients and varying parameter scales, but risk instability in regions of low curvature due to excessive step sizes. We introduce Eva (Escaping Via Adaptive gradients), a family of novel optimizers comprising two variants—Eva $$^{+}$$ + and Eva $$^{-}$$ - —that dynamically switch between Adam and scaled gradient steps based on local gradient and curvature properties. Our method implements component-wise detection to identify updates where Adam step magnitude exceeds the historical gradient norm. Eva $$^{+}$$ + employs gradient ascent to escape from degenerate regions, while Eva $$^{-}$$ - provides conservative descent with magnitude damping. We set a threshold for detecting unstable updates, supported by theoretical analysis and empirical validation. Extensive experiments prove that both Eva variants achieve faster convergence and improved generalization compared to popular optimizers.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Computer Networking and Communication Protocols in the Digital Era
venue: Proceedings of International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Networks
abstract: The rapid evolution of the digital technologies has significantly made a difference in the computer networking and communication protocol that resulted in the unprecedented connectivity, scale, and interoperability. This survey provides a profound understanding of the key trends and current trends in computer networking including the popularity of the next-generation Internet protocols, integration of Internet of Things (IoT) systems, the emergence of quantum and optical communication models. It examines how security or privacy and interoperability have become more significant in different digital ecosystems such as smart cities, industrial automation, the metaverse and the Internet of Underwater Things. The paper categorizes the basic and emerging protocols based on the applications area, solves the problems, such as latency, bandwidth optimization and cyber threats, and refers to the state-of-the-art solutions, like blockchain, machine learning-based network optimization and software-defined networking. Additionally, the survey demonstrates the forthcoming directions of the networking paradigms in 6G, AI-assisted, and cyber-physical systems era and presents the research gaps and practical implications of researchers and industry stakeholders.

title: Model-Based Architecture Design and Safety Analysis of Distributed Electric Propulsion Systems for eVTOL
venue: Proceedings of The 2025 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Aerospace Technology Vol 5
abstract: The rapid development of Urban Air Mobility (UAM) has accelerated advancements in electric Vertical Take-Off and Landing (eVTOL) aircraft, where Distributed Electric Propulsion (DEP) systems play a critical role in achieving high efficiency, redundancy, and maneuverability. Unlike conventional propulsion architectures, DEP systems distribute multiple lift-thrust units across the airframe, featuring inherent fault tolerance. However, under stringent aviation certification standards, managing distributed propulsion components—particularly in system design, real-time decision-making, and safety certification—poses significant challenges. Building on the development of a six-rotor eVTOL aircraft, this study explores airworthiness-oriented DEP system design to meet safety requirements. At the component level, a hierarchical switching management architecture between the flight control computer and dual-winding master–slave Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor controllers is proposed to address the design limitations of COTS products, enabling autonomous failure detection, mode switching, and system recovery. At the system level, a triple-redundant CAN bus communication topology is constructed to ensure fault-tolerant operation. Subsequently, a safety analysis model incorporating fault injection and state transition logic is established to achieve qualitative and quantitative evaluation of system safety, demonstrating that the architectural design complies with airworthiness regulatory requirements.

title: Understanding the Robustness of BERT Models Against Hardware Errors: An Experimental Study
abstract: As deep neural network (DNN) based natural language processing (NLP) models continue to grow in scale and complexity, the hardware systems supporting them are becoming increasingly intricate and sophisticated. This complexity leads to a higher likelihood of hardware errors that pose significant threats to the reliability and performance of NLP services. In this experimental study, we investigate the robustness of BERT models in the presence of hardware errors, which can corrupt model parameters stored in memory. Our study involves an extensive error injection campaign targeting four widely-used BERT models, evaluated across six benchmarks spanning three diverse application domains. Additionally, we demonstrate that applying parameter clipping techniques can significantly enhance the error tolerance of BERT models, achieving up to $$100\times $$ 100 × improvement in robustness against hardware errors. Beyond error tolerance, we also explore the implications of these findings for energy-efficient hardware design, focusing specifically on SRAM. By combining SRAM voltage scaling techniques with the improved error tolerance of BERT models, we achieve average energy savings of up to 62.9%, with minimal impact on the performance of BERT models. Our results highlight the potential for optimizing hardware systems to support both reliable and energy-efficient execution of BERT models. The tool we developed for error injection is open-sourced at https://github.com/Raisony/Hugging-Error .

title: A Fairness-Aware Multi-agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient for Dynamic Scheduling
abstract: Dynamic scheduling is critical for enhancing performance, resource utilization, and adaptability in complex computational and industrial systems, especially within networked and cybersecurity environments where fairness and security are paramount. While the Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) algorithm demonstrates strong performance in decentralized scheduling, it often suffers from incentive conflicts among agents, leading to unfair resource allocation and instability during policy learning—issues that are particularly acute in networked systems prone to adversarial behaviors and security threats. To address these challenges, we propose Fair-MADDPG, a novel extension that seamlessly integrates fairness constraints into the policy gradient update. This approach ensures an equitable reward distribution among agents, thus promoting both robust system-level optimization and resilience against potential security vulnerabilities arising from unfair collaboration. Extensive experiments on eight diverse and challenging scheduling benchmarks, including scenarios inspired by network resource allocation and secure multi-agent coordination, demonstrate that Fair-MADDPG consistently achieves high task completion rates. Compared to state-of-the-art baselines, our method reduces decision latency by up to 67% and yields total rewards 3 to 36 times higher than MADPG, DQN, and Q-learning, all while maintaining inter-agent reward variance below 2%, thus ensuring fairness and stability.

title: Artificial Intelligence Control in Power Electronics
venue: Modern Control Methods for Power Electronics
abstract: This chapter explores the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the control of power electronic systems, addressing the increasing complexity and dynamic behavior of modern energy infrastructures. It systematically introduces and compares major AI paradigms such as Symbolic AI, Computational Intelligence (CI), Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and Reinforcement Learning (RL), emphasizing their unique contributions to modeling, control, and optimization in nonlinear, uncertain, and real-time environments. The discussion includes a detailed evaluation of algorithmic structures, strengths, and limitations of each approach in the context of power converters control, with a focus on control robustness, adaptability, and computational feasibility. Moreover, the chapter presents a comprehensive case study on RL-based current control of a grid-connected multilevel inverter, highlighting its capacity for model-free learning and real-time adaptation under varying operating conditions. This chapter serves as both a theoretical primer and a practical guide, equipping readers with foundational knowledge and design insights necessary for leveraging AI to advance intelligent and resilient power electronics systems in renewable energy and smart grid applications.

title: Machine Learning Control in Power Electronics
venue: Modern Control Methods for Power Electronics
abstract: Power electronic devices are fundamental components of modern technological developments due to play a critical role in management, conversion, and control of electrical energy. In the context of cutting-edge technology, these devices are crucial in enabling a wide range of applications. To accomplish such a pivotal role, a paradigm shift is also required in the control of power electronic devices. In this manner, advanced control of power electronic devices has a major role for achieving high dynamic performance, minimizing energy losses, enhancing system robustness, facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources, and smart grid technologies. Therefore, machine learning (ML) control based strategies have prominent features in control of power electronic systems. The main objective of this chapter is to provide a thorough and in-depth analysis of ML methods that applicable to the control of power electronic systems. Through detailed analysis, the significant potential of these approaches in advancing the future development of control and optimization in power electronic systems is explained.

title: Multimodal Collaborative Object Localization
venue: Multimodal Collaborative Perception for Unmanned Systems
abstract: This chapter examines collaborative object localization, a distributed perception paradigm in which multiple agents–such as vehicles, sensors, or viewpoints—cooperate to improve localization accuracy and robustness. Traditional single-agent localization methods often struggle in dynamic, cluttered, or partially observable environments due to limited field of view and sensing uncertainty. To address these limitations, collaborative strategies enable information sharing, coordinated communication, and joint spatial reasoning across networked agents. The chapter introduces foundational principles of collaborative localization and surveys representative frameworks, including multi-view geometry, multi-sensor fusion systems, and learning-based cooperative architectures. It further discusses recent advances in deep neural networks that support collaborative inference while highlighting practical challenges such as communication overhead, uncertainty propagation, and coordination under limited supervision. Application examples in autonomous driving, robotics, and security monitoring illustrate the practical benefits of cooperative localization. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open research problems and future directions in distributed perception systems.

title: Introduction to Multimodal Collaborative Perception
venue: Multimodal Collaborative Perception for Unmanned Systems
abstract: This chapter introduces collaborative perception for unmanned systems operating in dynamic, uncertain, and safety-critical environments. It begins by analyzing the limitations of traditional single-vehicle perception, including spatial occlusion, performance degradation in adverse conditions, limited sensing range, and tight coupling between perception and decision modules. These constraints can lead to incomplete environmental awareness and elevated safety risks in complex traffic scenarios. To address these challenges, collaborative perception is presented as a distributed framework that enables real-time data sharing and coordinated processing among vehicles, roadside infrastructure, and aerial platforms. The chapter explains its three integration levels—data, feature, and decision fusion—and emphasizes the importance of multi-source heterogeneity, precise spatial–temporal alignment, and adaptive fusion strategies for improving robustness and coverage. The evolution from single-sensor systems to onboard multi-sensor fusion and finally to networked collaborative architectures is outlined to provide research context. The chapter concludes by summarizing the structure of the book, covering foundational data processing, core estimation and perception algorithms, and system-level applications, thereby establishing a comprehensive framework for understanding collaborative perception technologies.

title: To Be, Not to Be, or Both: A Quantum Leap for Sentiment Analysis
venue: Advanced Network Technologies and Intelligent Computing
abstract: Sentiment analysis remains a fundamental yet challenging task in Natural Language Processing (NLP), especially when dealing with complex linguistic features like irony and sarcasm. Classical models, including transformers such as BERT, often struggle with these nuances. Quantum Natural Language Processing (QNLP) offers a novel approach by leveraging quantum mechanics to enhance language representation and classification. We propose the Quantum Entangled Contextual Sentiment Analysis (QECSA) model, a hybrid quantum-classical framework combining classical preprocessing and embeddings with a quantum classifier, Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC). QECSA encodes ambiguous word meanings using quantum superposition and captures contextual dependencies via entanglement in quantum circuits. We hypothesize that QECSA will demonstrate significant performance improvement over BERT, particularly in detecting irony and sarcasm, as measured by accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score on benchmark datasets. Additionally, our architecture achieves a latent reduction of nearly 40% when processing complex sentences in real-world applications. While current quantum hardware limits scalability, our hybrid approach leverages simulators and noise-resilient designs to demonstrate feasibility, laying the foundation for more expressive and context-aware sentiment analysis systems as quantum technology advances.

title: SA-IDS: a self-supervised and adaptive intrusion detection system for edge-based IIoT security with label-free drift resilience
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) introduces significant cybersecurity challenges due to resource constraints, the lack of labeled data, and evolving attack patterns. Existing intrusion detection systems (IDS) often rely on supervised learning and centralized retraining, which limits their applicability in real-world edge environments.In this paper, we propose SA-IDS, a self-supervised and adaptive intrusion detection framework designed for resource-constrained IIoT edge devices. The proposed model leverages contrastive self-supervised learning to learn robust representations of benign telemetry data without requiring labeled attacks. Anomaly detection is performed using the Mahalanobis distance in the learned embedding space, enabling effective identification of unseen threats. To address concept drift, a lightweight unsupervised adaptation mechanism is introduced, allowing continuous model updates using high-confidence benign samples.The proposed system is evaluated on a real-world IIoT testbed consisting of Raspberry Pi and ESP32 devices. Experimental results demonstrate that SA-IDS achieves a detection accuracy of 96.3%, an F1-score of 0.92, and a low false positive rate of 3.1%, outperforming several state-of-the-art baselines while maintaining real-time performance on edge devices.

title: Systematic review of artificial intelligence for thermal and fault state estimation in electric motor drives
abstract: Electric motor drives are increasingly used in electric vehicles, industrial automation, robotics, renewable energy systems, aerospace actuators, and smart manufacturing. Their reliable operation requires accurate fault diagnosis, robust thermal supervision, and timely health state estimation under variable operating conditions. Artificial intelligence and deep learning models have been widely applied to induction motor fault diagnosis, permanent magnet synchronous motor fault detection, demagnetization assessment, inverter fault diagnosis, anomaly detection, and temperature prediction. However, many studies still emphasize model accuracy while giving limited attention to dataset transparency, validation reliability, data leakage, operating-profile dependency, and real-time deployment constraints. This paper systematically reviews AI-enabled thermal and fault state estimation methods for electric motor drives, with emphasis on permanent magnet synchronous motors and induction motors. Studies are compared by motor platform, monitoring target, signal modality, model family, dataset source, validation design, leakage-control evidence, generalization setting, and implementation feasibility. Particular attention is given to train-test contamination mechanisms in correlated motor time series, including window overlap, preprocessing fitted before data separation, operating-profile overlap, and feature-selection leakage. The synthesis indicates that trustworthy motor monitoring depends less on isolated accuracy gains than on transparent datasets, group-aware validation, training-only preprocessing, evaluation under unseen conditions, physically credible modeling, and reporting of hardware-relevant metrics. The review concludes with a research agenda for integrated thermal-fault monitoring that combines robust validation, interpretable learning, compact models, and real-time motor-drive deployment.

title: From qubits to rhythm: exploring quantum random walks in rhythmspaces
venue: The European Physical Journal Special Topics
abstract: Abstract A quantum computing algorithm applied to rhythm generation is presented, which maps simulated quantum random walk trajectories onto a rhythmspace – a 2D interface that interpolates rhythmic patterns. The methodology consists of three stages. The first stage involves designing the quantum computing circuits and establishing a mapping between the qubit space and the rhythmspace . To minimize circuit depth, a decomposition of a 2D quantum random walk into two 1D quantum random walks is applied. The second stage focuses on biasing the directionality of quantum random walks by introducing various classical potential fields, adjusting the probability distribution of the wave function based on the position gradient within these fields. The third stage addresses the sonification of these paths by generating MIDI drum pattern messages and transmitting them to a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW). This work serves as a proof of concept for scalable quantum computing-based generative random walk algorithms in music and audio applications. Graphical abstract

title: Multi-sensor data-driven intelligent product interaction fault self-diagnosis system
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis is crucial for the safety and reliability of dynamic smart manufacturing systems. Existing single-sensor approaches do not model complex, multi-dimensional interactions between robotic components during dynamic interactions. This paper introduces a Kronecker Fused Variational-Evolutionary Reconstruction Framework for Adaptive Intelligent Diagnostics (KROVER-AID), which enables real-time, cross-sensor, and across-sensor fault diagnosis. The Kronecker fusion method captures the high-order cross-dependencies among vibration, current and torque signals to generate unified and discriminative feature embeddings. UNVAE (Unified Nested Variational Autoencoder) serves as a nested encoder-decoder to uncover latent fault features and accurately reconstruct fused representations, thus exposing subtle faults. UNVAE is trained by ERM (Evolutionary Reconstruction Model) using adaptive evolutionary optimization to fine-tune the parameters of the decoder, thus reducing the reconstruction error and improving the adaptability to unseen fault cases. Experimental validation on industrial-scale electric motor datasets with variable load and speed conditions shows that KROVER-AID outperforms the benchmark approaches by 6.5% in fault detection accuracy and 5.8% in F1-score. The proposed framework has demonstrated significant robustness, cross-domain generalization, and autonomous adaptability; therefore, it is a scalable and intelligent approach to predictive maintenance and fault management in next-generation smart manufacturing systems.

title: A3SM: Closed-loop anomaly-aware migration scheduling for gray failure mitigation in cloud clusters
abstract: Gray failures in cloud clusters often remain operational but degraded, making them difficult to handle with static alarms or failure-only recovery strategies. The main difficulty is not only detecting weak anomalies, but also deciding when to intervene, at what granularity to intervene, and where to place the affected workload under migration-cost constraints. To address this detection-to-mitigation gap, this paper proposes A3SM, a closed-loop anomaly-aware migration scheduling framework based on hierarchical reinforcement learning. A3SM combines four complementary detectors—Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) residual prediction, autoencoder reconstruction, Robust Principal Component Analysis (RPCA), and graph-consistency analysis—to obtain gray-failure risk scores. It further introduces task-level, node-level, and group-level attribution to localize the impact scope of anomalies before generating actions. On this basis, a two-level policy decouples intervention triggering from target-node selection, while an online benefit–cost feedback mechanism adaptively updates scheduling sensitivity and decision policies. Trace-driven experiments on Alibaba Cluster Trace 2017 show that A3SM achieves an anomaly-detection F1-score of 0.82, reduces the Res-SLO violation rate to 3.2%, and shortens the average recovery time to 185 s, while also reducing unnecessary migrations. Additional trace-driven validation on Google Borg Trace 2020 (F1 $$=$$ 0.79, Res-SLO violation rate 3.8%, MTTR 202 s) provides further evidence that the framework transfers across the two evaluated cluster traces. Within the limits of trace replay and controlled fault injection, these results suggest that closed-loop anomaly-aware scheduling can improve recovery timeliness and operational stability for gray-failure mitigation in cloud clusters.

title: A robust autonomous UAV obstacle avoidance through multi-sensor fusion and intelligent decision-making
abstract: With the development of smart cities, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become essential for applications such as crowd monitoring, infrastructure inspection, emergency response, traffic monitoring and urban surveillance. However, fully autonomous UAV navigation in metropolitan environments still faces significant challenges due to Global Positioning System (GPS) spoofing or dynamic obstacles. There have been various approaches proposed to mitigate these limitations, such as multisensor fusion and machine learning based perception. However, suffering substantial computation burdens in these current frameworks constrains real-time and interpretable decision making under uncertainty. This paper presents a novel multisensor fusion framework to address these constraints for UAV navigation in urban contexts. The system integrates a Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) driven GPS spoofing detection module for identifying spoofed signals. Once an anomaly is detected, the proposed model engages a multisensor fusion process to ensure reliable navigation in case of degraded GPS performance while maximizing computational efficiency. To further enhance the degree of autonomy, Logical Neural Networks (LNNs) are embedded to provide interpretable and context aware decision making and robust obstacle avoidance. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets establish that the proposed framework significantly improves navigation integrity, system robustness and decision transparency. Quantitatively, the framework achieves an overall accuracy of 90% with 75% emergency recall and 90% F1-score, outperforming other interpretable baselines while reducing inference load by 122.5 $$\times $$ through keyframe extraction.

title: Classifier chains for multi-label learning: a systematic review and taxonomy
abstract: Classifier chains (CC) have become one of the most influential paradigms for multi-label classification since their introduction in 2009. By chaining binary classifiers so that each exploits predictions of its predecessors as additional features, CC offer a principled yet practical mechanism for modeling label dependencies. Despite sustained research interest—with over 200 published works—a systematic-review treatment of this literature has not previously been published. This paper presents a PRISMA-compliant systematic review of classifier chains covering 2009–2026, complementing the perspectives article of Read et al. (JAIR, 2021 ) and the inference-method survey of Mena et al. ( 2016 ). The review is organized around four research questions covering the design space of CC variants, their empirical comparison under a common protocol, their theoretical properties (error propagation, optimality of greedy inference, role of chain order), and the most promising research frontiers. We propose a three-axis taxonomy that organizes CC variants along dependency modeling , inference strategy , and computational profile , and reorganize the analytical review along the algorithmic dimensions of chain order, ensemble strategy, chain structure, and base-classifier learning. Concretely, we contribute (i) a computational-complexity comparison of 18 CC variants, (ii) original reproducible experiments on nine datasets with eight metrics and Wilcoxon signed-rank statistical-significance testing, (iii) a formal treatment of error propagation and a summary of theoretical results on CC, (iv) a discussion of CC for cross-paradigm problems (multi-output regression, multi-dimensional classification, positive–unlabelled multi-label), (v) a source-code availability inventory, and (vi) an analysis of 23 application domains. We discuss seven research directions including integration with large language models, extreme multi-label scalability, and fairness-aware chain construction, and we state the scope limitations of this review explicitly.

title: Deployment-Oriented Deep Learning for Predictive Maintenance of Electric Motor-Driven Rotating Systems: A Review of Robustness, Trustworthiness, and Industrial Readiness
venue: Arabian Journal for Science and Engineering
abstract: Recent developments in predictive maintenance (PdM) for motor-driven rotating systems have improved fault detection, fault diagnosis, anomaly detection, and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. Despite this progress, industrial deployment remains constrained by scarce labeled data, variable operating conditions, noise, domain shift, computational and energy limits, privacy requirements, and the need for trustworthy decision support. This review examines deployment-oriented deep learning for electric motor-driven rotating systems, with electric motors treated as the central electromechanical assets and bearings, shafts, gears, and coupled loads considered as mechanically coupled subsystems. The review combines a structured literature mapping with a challenge-driven synthesis of 119 recent research papers and 30 review papers, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, and is organized around three key themes: data and model efficiency, reliability and generalization, and system-level integration. The literature is organized around data-efficient learning, robust and generalizable models, lightweight and deployable architectures, explainability and uncertainty quantification, foundation models, large language model-assisted frameworks, multi-sensor fusion, and federated learning. By linking methodological advances to practical deployment constraints, this review identifies the current maturity of recent PdM methods, clarifies the remaining gap between benchmark validation and industrial readiness, and outlines research priorities for robust, scalable, and trustworthy PdM solutions in motor-driven powertrain systems.

title: Agentic AI-driven IPv6 route lookup: a deterministic approach for low-altitude economy networks
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI)-driven low-altitude economy (LAE) networks require high forwarding throughput together with controlled route-update overhead. Large unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms may concentrate longest-prefix-match (LPM) queries at a small number of operationally common IPv6 prefix lengths, particularly /48 aggregation and /64 subnet prefixes. This paper proposes a distribution-aware heuristic binary search (HBS) scheme that uses empirical prefix-length probabilities and entropy to construct an asymmetric search structure. Marker projection and precomputed heuristic search paths (HSPs) preserve LPM correctness without lookup backtracking, while an associated marker list (AML) localizes the marker dependencies affected by route changes. A sliding-window mechanism rebalances the structure when persistent workload changes satisfy the configured triggers. In the evaluated Linux-server benchmark with four forwarding information base datasets and a Zipfian workload, HBS reaches 29.2 million lookups per second (MLPS) on the Cloud dataset and has an average update latency of 0.44 $$\mu \textrm{s}$$ across the four datasets; the corresponding Poptrie and Splitting Approach to Internet Protocol Lookup (SAIL) averages are 11.6 and 4.1 $$\mu \textrm{s}$$ . These measurements demonstrate favorable average performance under the evaluated configuration.

title: Intelligent phase change material envelopes for adaptive and predictive energy storage in smart buildings
abstract: Phase change materials (PCMs) can substantially reduce building energy demand through latent thermal energy storage, but conventional systems are constrained by passive operation and limited adaptability to varying climate, occupancy, and grid conditions. This field has been driven forward by recent advances in adaptive PCMs, predictive control, artificial intelligence, and digital twins, but the existing reviews cover these developments separately. This review summarizes 102 studies published from 2003 to 2026 and proposes a unified three-pillar framework of Hardware Intelligence, Control Intelligence and Data Intelligence for intelligent PCM building envelopes. It is demonstrated that passive PCM systems are inherently constrained by seasonal mismatch, and experimentally confirmed energy savings are on the order of 10–25%. However, with the integration of adaptive hardware and predictive control, reductions in operating cost of 20–57% and peak load shifting of up to 80% are possible. Emerging techniques such as reinforcement learning and differentiable predictive control provide improved adaptability but need more substantial experimental validation. The review concludes that the performance of intelligent PCM depends on the coordinated integration of material, control and data, rather than on isolated technological advances. Integrated material-control co-design, physics-informed artificial intelligence, digital twins and standardized evaluation frameworks are the critical priorities to accelerate grid-interactive, low-carbon building envelopes.

title: Enhanced IoT malware detection via robust and scalable federated learning
venue: Journal of Computer Virology and Hacking Techniques
abstract: With the rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) networks, securing connected devices against malware has become a critical challenge. Traditional centralised malware detection approaches often suffer from limitations related to data privacy, communication efficiency, and scalability. To address these issues, this work proposes a decentralised federated learning (FL)-based IoT malware detection framework, evaluated using the recent IoT-23 dataset and systematically assessed in terms of robustness and scalability. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves a strong baseline detection accuracy of 99.54% while incurring a communication overhead of only 0.49 MB, making it suitable for deployment in large-scale and resource-constrained IoT environments. The robustness of the framework was also evaluated under multiple adversarial scenarios, including label flipping, gradient manipulation, and targeted backdoor attack. In all these scenarios, the detection accuracy remained high (above 98%). The scalability experiments demonstrated negligible degradation in performance as the dataset size and number of participating clients were varied. More advanced experiments revealed minimal impact on performance when the number of clients and the type of aggregator were varied in adversarial settings, with accuracy remaining above 99.5% and 99.4%, respectively. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective, communication-efficient solution for large-scale IoT malware detection, highlighting the feasibility of robust and scalable FL-based security systems in real-world IoT deployments.

title: An integrated fuzzy Delphi–FANP framework for maintenance strategy design and manufacturing process improvement: a case study of Kombolcha steel products industry
venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
abstract: Designing a maintenance strategy is crucial for raising manufacturing performance, decreasing downtime, and increasing equipment reliability. Reactive maintenance is the primary method used by Kombolcha Steel Products Industry (KOSPI), which leads to frequent failures and higher maintenance expenses. This study creates an integrated framework for manufacturing process improvement and maintenance plan selection using the Fuzzy Delphi Method (FDM) and Fuzzy Analytic Network Process (FANP). Eighty respondents provided information via surveys, interviews, observations, and corporate documents. Key maintenance criteria were determined using FDM, and maintenance options were ranked by FANP. With priority weights of 0.497, 0.285, 0.142, and 0.077, respectively, the findings indicate that preventive maintenance is the most favored approach, followed by predictive, condition-based, and corrective maintenance. The suggested architecture enhances manufacturing performance and facilitates methodical maintenance decision-making.

title: From graphs to qubits: a critical review of quantum graph neural networks
abstract: Quantum Graph Neural Networks represent a novel fusion of quantum computing and Graph Neural Networks, aimed at overcoming the computational and scalability challenges inherent in classical models that are powerful tools for analyzing data with complex relational structures but suffer from limitations such as high computational complexity and over-smoothing in large-scale applications. Quantum computing, leveraging principles like superposition and entanglement, offers a pathway to enhanced computational capabilities. This paper critically reviews the state-of-the-art in Quantum Graph Neural Networks, exploring various architectures. We discuss their applications across diverse fields such as high-energy physics, molecular chemistry, finance and earth sciences, highlighting the potential for quantum advantage. Additionally, we address the significant challenges faced by Quantum Graph Neural Networks, including noise, decoherence, and scalability issues, proposing potential strategies to mitigate these problems. This comprehensive review aims to provide a foundational understanding of Quantum Graph Neural Networks, fostering further research and development in this promising interdisciplinary field.

title: Fault diagnosis in incremental learning: an overview of technologies and industrial practices
abstract: With the continuous improvement of the intelligence level of industrial systems, equipment fault diagnosis in dynamic environments is confronted with issues such as the emergence of new fault modes and data distribution shift. Traditional batch training models struggle to adapt to various persistent changes. Incremental learning can integrate new data without forgetting acquired knowledge, offering a groundbreaking solution for the field of fault diagnosis. This paper systematically reviews the research progress of incremental learning in fault diagnosis. First, it introduces the basic theories of incremental learning and categorizes it into class-incremental, domain-incremental, task-incremental, and data-incremental learning. Second, it analyzes the practical applications of regularization, dynamic architecture, memory replay, and meta-learning techniques in incremental learning scenarios. Finally, it prospects future research directions including open-set incremental diagnosis and interpretable incremental learning. This review intends to serve as a reference for researchers in this field and advance the development of incremental fault diagnosis.

title: A quantum reservoir computing approach to quantum stock price forecasting in technology-markets
abstract: We present a quantum reservoir computing (QRC) framework based on a small-scale quantum system comprising at most six interacting qubits, designed for nonlinear financial time-series forecasting. We apply the model to predict future daily closing trading prices of 20 quantum-sector publicly traded companies over the period from April 11, 2020, to April 11, 2025 (exclusive), as well as minute-by-minute trading prices during out-of-market hours on July 7, 2025. Our analysis identifies optimal reservoir parameters that yield stock trend (up/down) classification accuracies exceeding 86%. Importantly, the QRC model is platform-agnostic and can be realized across diverse physical implementations of qubits, including superconducting circuits and trapped ions. These results demonstrate the expressive power and robustness of small-scale quantum reservoirs for modeling complex temporal correlations in financial data, highlighting their potential applicability to real-world forecasting tasks on near-term quantum hardware.

title: Quantum circuit-based learning models: bridging quantum computing and machine learning
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) has been widely applied across numerous domains due to its ability to automatically identify informative patterns from data for various tasks. The availability of large-scale data and advanced computational power enables the development of sophisticated models and training strategies, leading to state-of-the-art performance, but it also introduces substantial challenges. Quantum Computing (QC), which exploits quantum mechanisms for computation, has attracted growing attention and significant global investment as it may address these challenges. Consequently, Quantum Machine Learning (QML), the integration of these two fields, has received increasing interest, with a notable rise in related studies in recent years. We are motivated to review these existing contributions regarding quantum circuit-based learning models for classical data analysis and highlight the identified potentials and challenges of this technique. Specifically, we focus not only on QML models, both kernel-based and neural network-based, but also on recent explorations of their integration with classical machine learning layers within hybrid frameworks. Moreover, we examine both theoretical analysis and empirical findings to better understand their capabilities, and we also discuss the efforts on noise-resilient and hardware-efficient QML that could enhance its practicality under current hardware limitations. In addition, we cover several emerging paradigms for advanced quantum circuit design and highlight the adaptability of QML across representative application domains.
